17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

17:24.ar: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
17:24.en: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little

pwHiG5oMrqI.speaker: adnan
pwHiG5oMrqI.speaker_note: episode 5 of his Ramadan series; refers to the centre he started, his hospital work and growing up in Syria and Saudi Arabia
pwHiG5oMrqI.title: Chastity, Love and Gender Relations (Reduced Concepts, Episode 5)
pwHiG5oMrqI.one_line: Chastity reduced to a headscarf, haya to shyness, love to lust, and gender relations to sex: recovering the fuller concepts and their boundaries.
pwHiG5oMrqI.summary: He takes on three sensitive concepts. Chastity has been reduced to hijab, and hijab to a piece of cloth, which overloads sisters and leaves men out of the conversation entirely, though the Prophet counselled young men about marriage and spoke to men and women separately in ways that should not be turned into leverage. Hijab means boundaries: a social system covering dress, speech and conduct for both genders, so fully walled-off masjids avoid the problem rather than training youth. Haya comes from the root for life and means heightened sensitivity to how one affects others, not bashfulness; it is the defining ethic of Islam. Such a system values people by merit rather than appearance and acknowledges human nature openly. Love, the long-term motive behind lasting faith, has been confused with lust, which has its place in marriage. He challenges the myth of 'the one', jealousy of a spouse's love for family, the sexualising of male friendship, and 'fish love' that values people only for what they provide, as when elderly parents become disposable. Love is not only an emotion; it needs proof and clear definitions. Finally, gender relations cannot be reduced to sex or identity; total segregation has failed, and what is forbidden is relationships without boundaries, while legitimate professional, educational and social relationships are fine within their limits.

outline.heading: Three concepts about relationships
outline.gist: Today covers chastity, love and gender relations, concepts as reduced as the rituals.

outline.heading: Chastity: know where we differ from the world
outline.gist: Abrahamic faiths understand sexuality differently from the modern world, and children must know where they part ways with peers, as they already do with food.

outline.heading: Chastity reduced to a piece of cloth
outline.gist: Reducing 'iffah to hijab and hijab to a headscarf makes one part carry the whole value, an impossible burden on sisters.

outline.heading: Hijab means boundaries, a social system
outline.gist: Hijab is a barrier: a social contract between Muslim men and women that includes a dress code for both genders.

outline.heading: Men left out of the conversation
outline.gist: Because hijab became a woman's garment, young men never get the talk; the Prophet counselled young men on marriage and family problems.

outline.heading: Private advice is not public leverage
outline.gist: Much of the Prophet's advice on marriage was given to men or women separately; spouses should not use the other gender's hadith against each other.

outline.heading: When the headscarf stands alone
outline.gist: Excluding men breeds bad behaviour toward women, and a scarf without the matching conduct backfires.

outline.heading: Total segregation runs from the problem
outline.gist: Masjids that wall genders off entirely avoid the issue instead of training people to share space respectfully.

outline.heading: Preparing youth for school and work
outline.gist: Running a centre has brought unexpected problems, but they show youth need guidance on conduct with the opposite gender.

outline.heading: Haya: not modesty but life
outline.gist: Haya comes from the root for life, and its form denotes the epitome of being alive.

outline.heading: Sensitivity, like a sternal rub
outline.gist: Life is shown by response to stimulus, so haya is the highest sensitivity; shyness or introversion is something else.

outline.heading: Aware of how you affect others
outline.gist: Haya is awareness of how one's words, dress, walk and presence affect people and the community.

outline.heading: How haya became 'modesty'
outline.gist: Sensitivity led to dressing appropriately, then the rest was dropped and only modesty remained.

outline.heading: The guest who overstays
outline.gist: A visitor who sits for hours oblivious to his host's signals lacks haya.

outline.heading: The Prophet: sensitive and brave
outline.gist: His haya was not weakness; he led armies and was always mindful of how he affected others.

outline.heading: Haya is the ethic of Islam
outline.gist: Every religion has a defining ethic and Islam's is haya: no blocking cars, wrecking washrooms, stepping over people or shoving at the doors after Jumuah.

outline.heading: Valued for merit, not appearance
outline.gist: Islam's dress and gaze norms shift attention from looks, which fade and are not earned, to what a person says and who they are.

outline.heading: Acknowledging human nature
outline.gist: Men and women differ in what attracts them; Islam organises society around that nature so both are safe and transgressors stand out.

outline.heading: The masjid's responsibility to teens
outline.gist: When a 14-year-old comes home from the masjid with a relationship, the community failed to make it a safe space.

outline.heading: The Prophet's masjid had no wall
outline.gist: Men prayed in front and women behind, and men waited until women had safely left before going out in the dark.

outline.heading: Early nights and afternoon naps
outline.gist: Village life with little electricity meant sleeping early; he values the midday nap and wishes days were structured around it.

outline.heading: Boundaries: you're not on the market yet
outline.gist: Dress, gaze and speech norms exist because desire will be sought too early without them; if you want marriage, ask properly and move on.

outline.heading: Dressing to be desired
outline.gist: A normalised phrase about dressing to attract reveals how far values have shifted; dress should express respect and values.

outline.heading: Hospitals more professional than masjids
outline.gist: Workplace codes of conduct often embody this ethic better than our masjids do.

outline.heading: Trust and gender-specific talks
outline.gist: Parents restrict children because they cannot trust them, since chastity was never properly discussed; these talks must be tailored to each gender.

outline.heading: Love versus lust
outline.gist: Islam is built on love, which he learned from teachers under siege in Syria, yet we confuse it with lust.

outline.heading: Lack of love behind reduced concepts
outline.gist: Practice driven only by discipline that fails its purpose becomes mechanical to resolve cognitive dissonance.

outline.heading: Fear, desire and discipline are short-term
outline.gist: These motives start the engine, but love is the endless long-term energy of being Muslim.

outline.heading: Lust has its place in marriage
outline.gist: Attraction is needed for marriage; marrying someone you are not attracted to is unfair to her.

outline.heading: Look before you propose
outline.gist: The Prophet told a man to look at the woman first, for her sake as much as his.

outline.heading: Love stories end at the altar
outline.gist: Romances stop at the wedding; divorces full of hatred show there was no love, and parting should be done with grace.

outline.heading: The myth of 'the one'
outline.gist: Among eight billion people we are capable of loving most; believing in a single destined person was a sold idea.

outline.heading: Jealousy of a spouse's love for family
outline.gist: Resenting a spouse's love for parents or siblings reflects insecurity; these loves differ in kind.

outline.heading: Love reduced to sexuality: holding hands
outline.gist: His grandmother assumed two men holding hands meant something sexual, yet friends in the Middle East did so innocently.

outline.heading: Confusing men about their friendships
outline.gist: Defining all love as sexual leads young men to question ordinary affection for friends.

outline.heading: Fish love
outline.gist: Loving fish means eating it; much love today values others only for what they give us, while media pushes ever more disturbing themes.

outline.heading: The Giving Tree and disposable parents
outline.gist: When parents have nothing left to give, some children wish them gone; traditional Muslim homes kept elders at the centre with dignity.

outline.heading: Love needs proof, not just emotion
outline.gist: Declaring love without action means nothing; emotions are your own to manage.

outline.heading: Men and women express love differently
outline.gist: Men often show love through lifelong provision and sacrifice, women in other ways.

outline.heading: Is love conditional?
outline.gist: If unconditional love means the emotion, that is impossible; feelings respond to how we are treated.

outline.heading: Unconditional love for Allah
outline.gist: Allah's gift of existence outweighs any lifetime of suffering, so our love for Him must not hinge on events.

outline.heading: Unconditional love for people needs definition
outline.gist: Loving a child who abuses you unconditionally raises questions of emotion versus care; vague terms leave people unsure when to let go.

outline.heading: Love is hard to define
outline.gist: Even scholars disagree on its definition, but it is not just emotion or sex, and claims about it need clear parameters.

outline.heading: Father and son drawing lots for battle
outline.gist: A companion would give his son anything except his place in the battle, since each must save himself from the Fire.

outline.heading: Don't accept the reduction of love
outline.gist: Love takes many forms, always with evidence and caregiving, sometimes with emotion; it deserves deep thought.

outline.heading: Discovering the gender conversation in the West
outline.gist: Only after moving here did he grasp how far the discussion of gender had gone.

outline.heading: Relations cannot be reduced to sex
outline.gist: Seeing every encounter with the opposite gender as potentially sexual hinders collaboration, creativity and growth, even for the married.

outline.heading: The male brain needs education
outline.gist: Left alone, male psychology sexualises every encounter; inhibition must be taught from a young age.

outline.heading: Gender as identity
outline.gist: Islam never asked people to declare what they are attracted to; that is private and not a basis for identity.

outline.heading: Islam organises relations for families
outline.gist: The aim is stable families that pass Islam on; making gender fluid empties the word of meaning and confuses people.

outline.heading: Sexuality is delicate
outline.gist: Exposure to the wrong things or abuse in childhood can damage a person's capacity for intimacy for life.

outline.heading: What is forbidden is the lack of boundaries
outline.gist: Flirtation and suggestive, unclear signals are the problem; men and women working together for the community is not.

outline.heading: Total segregation failed
outline.gist: Having grown up in Saudi Arabia, he sees today's upheaval there as the result of a society denied any education in dealing with the opposite gender.

outline.heading: Permissible relationships and their parameters
outline.gist: Teacher and student, co-workers, classmates, doctor and patient, neighbours and relatives each have limits; when someone leaves them, make intentions clear or return.

outline.heading: Outro

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

55:60.en: Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness

57:20.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱ وَزِينَةࣱ وَتَفَاخُرُۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَتَكَاثُرࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِۖ كَمَثَلِ غَيۡثٍ أَعۡجَبَ ٱلۡكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصۡفَرࣰّ ا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَٰمࣰ اۖ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣱۚ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
57:20.en: Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children; as the likeness of vegetation after rain, whereof the growth is pleasing to the husbandman, but afterward it drieth up and thou seest it turning yellow, then it becometh straw. And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion

57:21.ar: سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:21.en: Race one with another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whereof the breadth is as the breadth of the heavens and the earth, which is in store for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. Such is the bounty of Allah, which He bestoweth upon whom He will, and Allah is of Infinite Bounty

57:22.ar: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّبۡرَأَهَآۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣱ‏
57:22.en: Naught of disaster befalleth in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before we bring it into being - Lo! that is easy for Allah

57:23.ar: لِّكَيۡلَا تَأۡسَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَفۡرَحُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورٍ
57:23.en: That ye grieve not for the sake of that which hath escaped you, nor yet exult because of that which hath been given. Allah loveth not all prideful boasters

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
58:18.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together, then will they swear unto Him as they (now) swear unto you, and they will fancy that they have some standing. Lo! is it not they who are the liars

59:19.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ نَسُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
59:19.en: And be not ye as those who forgot Allah, therefor He caused them to forget their souls. Such are the evil-doers

55:13.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

59:22.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِۖ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
59:22.en: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah, the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible. He is the Beneficent, Merciful

59:23.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
59:23.en: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

SLeFku96JLY.speaker: adnan
SLeFku96JLY.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads; another speaker gives a short appeal at the end
SLeFku96JLY.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 26: Quranic Reflections (Al-Qamar 9 to the end of Al-Hashr)
SLeFku96JLY.one_line: Balancing form and spirit, the Madani organisational cluster, the Quran as blessing or curse, excellence answered with excellence, regret and vanity, self-deception, and forgetting Allah.
SLeFku96JLY.summary: He recaps the comparative surahs from Qaf to al-Hadid, stressing al-Hadid's demand to balance outward practice with inner spirituality, and laments that the ummah splits into people precise in the mechanics of the Sunnah but empty inside and spiritual people who neglect its form. He then introduces the Madani cluster from al-Mujadilah onward as the Quran's organisational summary: rules for worship, money and relationships within the community and between natives and newcomers, punctuated by concentrated spirituality so believers never forget why they follow the rules; forgetting the why turns religious work into us-against-them and breeds brutality, and no institution has value unless it serves Allah. Al-Qamar's refrain that the Quran is made easy to take to heart shows that an unused blessing backfires: nothing comes from Allah labelled, you decide whether it becomes a blessing. Ar-Rahman's question about the reward of excellence becomes an invitation to offer your best and receive His. Al-Hadid teaches that every calamity was decreed so you neither drown in regret nor grow vain over what you have. Al-Mujadilah warns of people so convinced of their own lies they will swear to Allah, and al-Hashr warns that those who forget Allah are made to forget themselves.

outline.heading: Opening
Memorise the Mufassal slowly
outline.gist: The last four juz summarise the first twenty-six; memorising about half a page a week brings the whole portion within a couple of years.

outline.heading: The comparative cluster recalled
outline.gist: Qaf to an-Najm set out contrasting values to choose between: righteousness or not, purpose or aimlessness, guidance or invention, knowledge or whims.

outline.heading: Al-Qamar: an unused blessing backfires
outline.gist: The punished nations were given prophethood, signs and guidance and refused them, so the blessing turned against them.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: gratitude keeps blessings
outline.gist: Its refrain asks which of Allah's favours the two addressees deny, whether jinn and humans or believers and disbelievers.

outline.heading: Al-Waqi'ah: three categories
outline.gist: What you do now decides which of the three groups you join on Judgment Day; two of the three make it.

outline.heading: Al-Hadid: opposites you must balance
outline.gist: As each cluster's last surah adds a twist, al-Hadid asks not to choose between spirit and matter, appearance and essence, but to hold both.

outline.heading: Mechanics without essence, spirit without Sunnah
outline.gist: One group perfects the outward details of prayer but lacks connection, another is spiritual but ignores the Sunnah's form; the Prophet's real legacy was closeness to Allah within a precise outward practice, which is why the most spiritual surah is called Iron.

outline.heading: The Madani juz: Islam organises life
outline.gist: Unlike the Makkan surahs around it, this juz is entirely Madani because the Quran's summary needed rules too; without fiqh everyone would improvise prayer and zakat and life would be chaos.

outline.heading: Al-Mujadilah: relationships within the Muslim community
outline.gist: It organises relations between Muslims, spouses, leaders and those not committed to the same cause on empathy, compassion, justice and equal value; it is named for the woman who argued her case to the Prophet.

outline.heading: Al-Hashr: citizenship between natives and newcomers
outline.gist: Like every country, Madinah had natives and immigrants, and the surah sets out the social and financial system for people sharing one land.

outline.heading: Concentrated doses of spirituality
outline.gist: Every two or three pages of rules, Allah places intense spirituality to remind you why you follow them; forget that and the means becomes the purpose and the system collapses.

outline.heading: Forget the why and it becomes us against them
outline.gist: We follow the rules because Allah commanded them, not for group identity or ego; in large community affairs losing that link turns disagreements into endless clashes with no goal.

outline.heading: Brutality comes from disconnecting acts from Allah
outline.gist: Holding your words and actions to Allah's standard brings sincerity; discrimination and loss of compassion come when people serve their own power and those like them.

outline.heading: No value in any institution that does not serve Allah
outline.gist: The juz's lists of Allah's names remind you who He is and why you do all this; a group, a masjid or Islam itself has no innate value unless it serves Allah and His people.

outline.heading: Interlude
Made easy to take to heart
outline.gist: Dhikr can mean remembrance, comprehension, memorisation or all of these; the word for one who takes heed describes someone moved to learn and internalise.

outline.heading: A refrain after every story of ruin
outline.gist: After each story that ends in punishment Allah repeats that the Quran is easy: will anyone learn? No? Then hear the next story.

outline.heading: Unused blessings backfire, even in worldly life
outline.gist: An advantage you never use weighs on you as you watch others do more with less, but what matters is that Allah's gift turns into something else if neglected.

outline.heading: Nothing from Allah comes labelled
outline.gist: You hold the label gun: what you are given becomes a blessing or a cause of punishment depending on what you do with it.

outline.heading: Even the Quran can become a curse
outline.gist: Many who heard it from the Prophet in their own pure Arabic, understanding it better than we do, still ended in Hell; ask Allah to make it a blessing in your life.

outline.heading: Interlude
Is excellence rewarded with anything but excellence?
outline.gist: First reading: having heard all the bounties of Paradise He has prepared, the fitting response is to show excellence yourself.

outline.heading: Show Me your excellence and I will show you Mine
outline.gist: Second reading: you kept getting up, repenting and never gave up; your resilience is met with His excellence.

outline.heading: Our best is mediocre, yet He pairs them
outline.gist: A self-aware person sees how his best lacks sincerity, compassion and grit; he would never dare mention it beside Allah's excellence had Allah not done so Himself.

outline.heading: Interlude
Life on instinct: play, distraction, rivalry
outline.gist: Worldly life lived on instinct is play, distraction, adornment and competing for more; Allah teaches that this is not how we are meant to live.

outline.heading: Every calamity was decreed before creation
outline.gist: Whatever hardship reaches you was written before life itself existed.

outline.heading: So you do not drown in sorrow over what you missed
outline.gist: Accept the past and learn from it rather than living in what-ifs; even after a terrible choice it is done, so take the lesson, seek mental health help when stuck, and hold to this religious reason to move on.

outline.heading: Interlude
Farah means vanity
outline.gist: In the Quran farah is vanity, not happiness: do not let status, wealth or achievements go to your head, for Allah does not love the vain and boastful.

outline.heading: Learn from the past, be grateful for the present
outline.gist: For what you lost, missed or messed up, learn and move on optimistically; for what you have, be grateful and humble and use it for Allah.

outline.heading: Swearing to Allah on Judgment Day
outline.gist: He picks the spiritual verses from these legal surahs; this one is among the ten most frightening to him: people swear to Allah Himself as they swore to others.

outline.heading: Believing your own lie
outline.gist: Lying to others or to yourself is one thing; believing your own lie until you lose touch with what is real is another.

outline.heading: You can beat a polygraph, not Allah
outline.gist: Allah sees exactly why and how you did what you did.

outline.heading: The undisclosed detail and the full replay
outline.gist: People hide the one detail that changes a dispute and convince themselves it changes nothing; Allah will replay it all, with the hidden intentions, showing where the first lie began.

outline.heading: Past the point of seeing your fault
outline.gist: Some go so far they lose the ability to see their fault, which is nearly beyond redemption; seek refuge in Allah from it.

outline.heading: They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves
outline.gist: Forgetting Allah does not mean not knowing Him; it means a life in which He is a side thought.

outline.heading: Allah on the bench
outline.gist: Religion sat on the bench for most of the year, showing up on the 27th night and Eid; even someone practising can forget Him when practice becomes self-serving and lost in technicalities.

outline.heading: Losing barakah and losing yourself
outline.gist: Projects not connected to Allah lose barakah; the consequence of forgetting Him is forgetting who you are and why you are here, the ultimate loss.

outline.heading: Unrecognisable to yourself in midlife
outline.gist: Many wake in their forties or fifties not knowing the person in the mirror or where their life is going, caught in a whirl with no time to reflect or renew intentions.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Appearance and essence: outward form mirroring the heart
themes.note: Islam needs both the Sunnah's outward form and its spiritual connection; the ummah keeps splitting them.

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: The Madani cluster organises worship, money and relationships; rules prevent chaos.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Remembering that rules and community work are for Allah keeps them sincere and humane; forgetting breeds factionalism and brutality.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is made easy to take to heart, yet it can become a curse for those who neglect it.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Unused or unthanked blessings turn against you; you decide the label.

themes.label: Ihsan and excellence in worship
themes.note: Excellence is answered with excellence; offer your imperfect best and receive Allah's.

themes.label: Belief in divine decree (qadar)
themes.note: Knowing calamities were decreed frees you from endless what-ifs.

themes.label: Mental health, anxiety and emotional wellbeing
themes.note: Getting stuck in regret can be crippling; seek help and use faith's reason to move on.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Do not let what you have make you vain; let it make you grateful.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Self-deception can grow until people swear falsely to Allah without realising they lie.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Forgetting Allah leads to forgetting yourself and losing your sense of who you are and why you are here.

The woman who argued her case, after whom the surah is named.
The succession of Allah's names at the end of the surah as a dose of spirituality amid legislation.

Forget why you do it and the means becomes the purpose
No institution has value unless it serves Allah
Show Me your excellence and I will show you Mine
It is another thing to believe your own lie
Allah on the bench, not an active player

stories.who: Those who heard the Quran from the Prophet in their own Arabic
stories.point: Understanding the Quran well does not make it a blessing unless you take it.

Muslim institutions and community disputes that lose sight of serving Allah

42:37.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُواْ هُمۡ يَغۡفِرُونَ
42:37.en: And those who shun the worst of sins and indecencies and, when they are wroth, forgive

3:134.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلۡكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
3:134.en: Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good

5:13.ar: فَبِمَا نَقۡضِهِم مِّيثَٰقَهُمۡ لَعَنَّٰهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَا قُلُوبَهُمۡ قَٰسِيَةࣰۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَنَسُواْ حَظࣰّ ا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِۦۚ وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَىٰ خَآئِنَةࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱصۡفَحۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
5:13.en: And because of their breaking their covenant, We have cursed them and made hard their hearts. They change words from their context and forget a part of that whereof they were admonished. Thou wilt not cease to discover treachery from all save a few of them. But bear with them and pardon them. Lo! Allah loveth the kindly

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy, and to fugitives for the cause of Allah. Let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

4YHx9_u4UQw.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 22: Tahajjud (Second Night)
4YHx9_u4UQw.one_line: Two tahajjud reminders: forgive people as you hope Allah forgives you, and in the last ten nights favour consistent deeds done with excellence.
4YHx9_u4UQw.summary: Two short reminders between the rakaat of this tahajjud night. The first is on forgiving people. He gathers the Quranic picture of pardon: believers who forgive even when angered (42:37), the muhsinin who pardon people and whom Allah loves (3:134), and the command to the Prophet to pardon and overlook (5:13), tying human pardon to Allah's own attribute of pardoning. He holds up Yusuf, who met the brothers who had wronged him with 'no blame on you today' (12:92), as the model. In the month of forgiveness he puts the question of 24:22 to the congregation: do you not love that Allah should forgive you? He adds that modern psychology points the same way about people who forgive. The second reminder, on entering the last ten nights, turns to how worship should be done: the Prophet named the most beloved deeds to Allah as the most consistent ones, even if small, and said Allah loves that a deed be done with excellence. The practical call is to pardon those who wronged you, and to choose deeds you can keep up and do them well.

outline.heading: Interlude
Believers forgive even when angered
outline.gist: He opens with the description of believers who, when angry, forgive (42:37).

outline.heading: Pardoning people as a mark of the muhsinin
outline.gist: Those who pardon people are among the doers of excellence whom Allah loves (3:134), and pardon is first an attribute of Allah Himself.

outline.heading: The Prophet commanded to pardon and overlook
outline.gist: Allah tells the Prophet to pardon and overlook, for Allah loves the muhsinin (5:13).

outline.heading: Yusuf forgives his brothers
outline.gist: Yusuf, after everything his brothers did, tells them there is no blame on them today (12:92): the model of full forgiveness.

outline.heading: Forgive as you hope to be forgiven
outline.gist: In Ramadan, the month of forgiveness, he asks whether we do not love that Allah forgive us (24:22), and notes that modern psychology also favours the forgiving.

outline.heading: Interlude
Entering the last ten nights
outline.gist: He turns the congregation toward the last ten nights of Ramadan and what they should bring to them.

outline.heading: The most beloved deeds are the most consistent
outline.gist: Aisha's narration: asked which deeds Allah loves most, the Prophet said the most consistent, even if small.

outline.heading: Allah loves a deed done with excellence
outline.gist: Allah loves that when one of you does a deed, he does it with itqan, so quality matters alongside consistency.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

Pardoning people is a quality of the muhsinin whom Allah loves.
The Prophet is commanded to pardon and overlook.
Yusuf tells his brothers there is no blame on them today.

Hold back anger and answer it with forgiveness, as the believers in 42:37 do.

47:15.ar: مَّثَلُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَۖ فِيهَآ أَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيۡرِ ءَاسِنࣲ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن لَّبَنࣲ لَّمۡ يَتَغَيَّرۡ طَعۡمُهُۥ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ خَمۡرࣲ لَّذَّةࣲ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ عَسَلࣲ مُّصَفࣰّ ىۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ كَمَنۡ هُوَ خَٰلِدࣱ فِي ٱلنَّارِ وَسُقُواْ مَآءً حَمِيمࣰ ا فَقَطَّعَ أَمۡعَآءَهُمۡ
47:15.en: A similitude of the Garden which those who keep their duty (to Allah) are promised: Therein are rivers of water unpolluted, and rivers of milk whereof the flavour changeth not, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of clear-run honey; therein for them is every kind of fruit, with pardon from their Lord. (Are those who enjoy all this) like those who are immortal in the Fire and are given boiling water to drink so that it teareth their bowels

48:26.ar: إِذۡ جَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَأَلۡزَمَهُمۡ كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهۡلَهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣰ ا
48:26.en: When those who disbelieve had set up in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of the Age of Ignorance, then Allah sent down His peace of reassurance upon His messenger and upon the believers and imposed on them the word of self-restraint, for they were worthy of it and meet for it. And Allah is Aware of all things

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

50:19.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
50:19.en: And the agony of death cometh in truth. (And it is said unto him): This is that which thou wast wont to shun

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

3:154.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةࣰ نُّعَاسࣰ ا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةࣰ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءࣱ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
3:154.en: Then, after grief, He sent down security for you. As slumber did it overcome a party of you, while (the other) party, who were anxious on their own account, thought wrongly of Allah, the thought of ignorance. They said: Have we any part in the cause? Say (O Muhammad): The cause belongeth wholly to Allah. They hide within themselves (a thought) which they reveal not unto thee, saying: Had we had any part in the cause we should not have been slain here. Say: Even though ye had been in your houses, those appointed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie. (All this hath been) in order that Allah might try what is in your breasts and prove what is in your hearts. Allah is Aware of what is hidden in the breasts (of men)

33:33.ar: وَقَرۡنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرࣰ ا
33:33.en: And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance. Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing

5:50.ar: أَفَحُكۡمَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ يَبۡغُونَۚ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ حُكۡمࣰ ا لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُوقِنُونَ
5:50.en: Is it a judgment of the time of (pagan) ignorance that they are seeking? Who is better than Allah for judgment to a people who have certainty (in their belief)

49:7.ar: وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِۚ لَوۡ يُطِيعُكُمۡ فِي كَثِيرࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ لَعَنِتُّمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَزَيَّنَهُۥ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ وَٱلۡفُسُوقَ وَٱلۡعِصۡيَانَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلرَّٰشِدُونَ
49:7.en: And know that the messenger of Allah is among you. If he were to obey you in much of the government, ye would surely be in trouble; but Allah hath endeared the faith to you and hath beautified it in your hearts, and hath made disbelief and lewdness and rebellion hateful unto you. Such are they who are the rightly guided

luUDRWtRp0s.speaker: adnan
luUDRWtRp0s.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads at his masjid
luUDRWtRp0s.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 25: Quranic Reflections (Muhammad to Al-Qamar 8)
luUDRWtRp0s.one_line: Following the Prophet as the condition for accepted deeds, the Mufassal's map of choices, never answering bigotry with bigotry, Islam versus iman, death, and minor slips.
luUDRWtRp0s.summary: He presents Muhammad, al-Fath and al-Hujurat as a short cluster about the Prophet: deeds count only when they follow his teaching, combat is mentioned because it is the hardest test of following him, al-Fath contrasts those who followed with those who did not, and al-Hujurat distils his etiquette. He then introduces the Mufassal, the last four juz that summarise the whole Quran, urges people to set a realistic goal of memorising them, and maps its first cluster as a sequence of choices: Paradise or Hell, purpose or aimlessness, guidance, knowledge over whims, gratitude for blessings, which of three groups to join, and balancing the spiritual with the physical. From Muhammad 15 he argues that choosing the Prophet's way should be easy because it brings peace here and Paradise after, and that Islam is no harder than making a child study. From al-Fath 26 he explains the zeal of ignorance as tribal partisanship and insists that Muslims never let oppressors drag them into answering bigotry with bigotry. Al-Hujurat 14 distinguishes saying Islam from internalised iman without licensing anyone to judge others. Qaf 19 confronts the certainty of death and how quickly we are forgotten, and an-Najm 32 reassures that avoiding major sins brings forgiveness for small slips.

outline.heading: Opening
A cluster about the Prophet; Muhammad: deeds accepted only by his way
outline.gist: Muhammad, al-Fath and al-Hujurat form one of the shortest clusters; deeds and a life count only if they accord with what the Prophet lived, taught and valued.

outline.heading: Why the Quran speaks of combat
outline.gist: No sane person longs for war and Muslims need not be defensive about it; combat is mentioned because it is the epitome of sacrifice, the hardest place to follow him when your life is on the line.

outline.heading: Al-Fath: followers and those who held back
outline.gist: The surah contrasts what those who followed the Prophet gained with what the others did, and its opening refers to Hudaybiyyah, not the conquest of Makkah, which it only foretells.

outline.heading: Interlude
Al-Hujurat: the Prophet's etiquette in two pages
outline.gist: Scholars urged teaching it to children early because it carries his manners, compassion, mercy, respect and kindness.

outline.heading: The Mufassal summarises the whole Quran
outline.gist: From Qaf to an-Nas, the detailed or comprehensive portion holds four clusters that restate in concise form everything the Quran has covered.

outline.heading: A realistic memorisation goal: the last four juz
outline.gist: Wanting the whole Quran is admirable, but a goal suited to your age and life is fine; steadily memorising the Mufassal over a couple of years beats ending with nothing.

outline.heading: The short surahs mirror the long ones
outline.gist: Almost every major topic of the Quran is mirrored in the Mufassal, which is why it is worth knowing and understanding well.

outline.heading: Qaf: Paradise or Hell
outline.gist: The comparative cluster opens with the ultimate question: do you care about living righteously and ending up in Paradise?

outline.heading: Adh-Dhariyat: purpose or aimlessness
outline.gist: Having chosen the Hereafter, will you live with a job to fulfil and meaning, or drift?

outline.heading: At-Tur: guidance or making up your own
outline.gist: Will you seek guidance, or live by an individual worldview of your own as much of humanity does?

outline.heading: An-Najm: knowledge or whims
outline.gist: Will you decide by authentic, referenced knowledge or by desires and assumptions?

outline.heading: Al-Qamar: blessings misused backfire
outline.gist: Blessings not used properly are taken away and turn into curses.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: blessings must be thanked
outline.gist: Gratitude keeps blessings coming and puts barakah in them.

outline.heading: Al-Waqi'ah: choose your group
outline.gist: There are three kinds of people and two of them make it; you must choose which you will be.

outline.heading: Al-Hadid: balance spirit and matter
outline.gist: Faith is both spiritual and physical, which is why one of the most spiritual surahs is named Iron; without that balance nothing works.

outline.heading: Short and comprehensive: every surah is a full unit
outline.gist: As surahs shorten toward the end of the Quran they grow more concise but remain complete units with equally weighty messages carrying all the values.

outline.heading: Interlude
Rivers that never spoil
outline.gist: Paradise has rivers of water that never turn stagnant and milk whose taste never changes.

outline.heading: Wine without losing sobriety
outline.gist: Recreationally removing your sobriety is forbidden; the drink of Paradise gives the joy people seek without headaches or loss of self-control.

outline.heading: Honey, fruit and forgiveness versus boiling water
outline.gist: Can the one enjoying these rivers, every fruit and his Lord's forgiveness be like the one given boiling water that tears his insides?

outline.heading: Why is following the Prophet a hard decision?
outline.gist: The rhetorical question shows the two outcomes are nothing alike; the Prophet only commanded what benefits you, so the choice should be simple.

outline.heading: Peace here and Paradise after
outline.gist: It would be a hard choice if following him meant agony in this life, but his teachings bring serenity and goodness now and Paradise later, while the other path offers only fleeting highs.

outline.heading: Islam is no harder than making a child study
outline.gist: Islam is hard only under persecution; as a system it is like pushing a nine-year-old to study instead of playing video games forever: unwelcome now, thanked for later.

outline.heading: Interlude
Four kinds of jahiliyyah in the Quran
outline.gist: The Quran uses the word four times, for problems of belief, behaviour, politics and ethics; the zeal of al-Fath is the ethical one.

outline.heading: Partisanship: siding with kin regardless of right
outline.gist: Hamiyyah means standing with whoever is closest to you, brother against cousin and cousin against stranger, with no regard for justice.

outline.heading: Quraysh barred the unarmed pilgrims
outline.gist: The Muslims came for umrah without weapons and were refused, something that historically had always led to war and to losing guardianship of Makkah.

outline.heading: Help your brother by stopping his oppression
outline.gist: The Prophet taught that you support an oppressing relative by holding him back, never by joining his wrongdoing because of blood.

outline.heading: Serenity and the word of taqwa
outline.gist: Allah sent tranquillity on the believers and bound them to the word of taqwa so they would not answer bigotry with bigotry; whoever started it, reciprocating puts you in the mud with them.

outline.heading: Hold your ethical ground against the oppressor
outline.gist: Oppressors want to pull you down so the lines blur and your claim weakens; being wrong because the other side is wrong was never acceptable at home, school or work, nor on a larger scale.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Bedouins who said we believe
outline.gist: Latecomers who joined after the heavy lifting expected equal status and claimed iman; Allah told them to say they had submitted, as iman had not yet entered their hearts.

outline.heading: Superficial and deep consciousness
outline.gist: What you believe but do not do sits at a superficial level, like knowing you should eat well or sleep early; what you believe and live by is iman.

outline.heading: Internalising takes reflection and change
outline.gist: Moving belief deeper requires contemplation and changes in lifestyle, companions and environment; obey Allah and His Messenger and none of your deeds will be diminished.

outline.heading: Iman dictates behaviour
outline.gist: Anyone can say the shahadah; iman is when values are internalised and steer how you live.

outline.heading: Only Allah can say who lacks iman
outline.gist: This verse is Allah speaking; no one may tell another they are not yet a believer, and he fears for his own iman, so use it to hold yourself accountable.

outline.heading: Heraclius and Abu Sufyan: no one leaves once iman mixes with the heart
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan, forced to be honest before the Roman ruler, admitted followers did not abandon the Prophet; Heraclius said that is how iman is once its joy enters the heart.

outline.heading: Ask Allah to make iman beloved
outline.gist: This is what we seek on these nights: that Allah make faith beloved and beautiful in our hearts so we never give it up.

outline.heading: Death comes for you, in fear and pain
outline.gist: We spend life running from death and it finds us; its stupor mixes fear and pain, with joy only in the believer's hope that what follows is better.

outline.heading: The one certainty
outline.gist: Death comes in truth as promised; in a hundred years no one in the room will be alive, and the community's future depends on what we do in the next few decades.

outline.heading: Forgotten within generations
outline.gist: You barely think of grandparents you loved; within a few generations your name becomes just another link in a lineage no one cares about.

outline.heading: What you have avoided all your life
outline.gist: Once you internalise this you stop clinging to what is not yours; we avoid even thinking of death, as he did as a child at an uncle's funeral.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those who avoid the major sins
outline.gist: Those who succeed avoid the cardinal sins and indecencies that violate integrity, such as murder, theft, lying, harming others and zina.

outline.heading: Lamam: the sweepings Allah forgives
outline.gist: Lamam is the residue left after sweeping: the near-unavoidable slips of word, glance and thought; your Lord's forgiveness encompasses them, so stay away from the big things.

themes.label: The Sunnah: what following the Prophet really means
themes.note: Deeds count only when they follow the Prophet's teaching; the cluster contrasts followers with those who held back.

themes.label: Combat in Islam and the ethics of defence
themes.note: Combat appears in the Quran as the ultimate test of sacrifice, not an encouragement of bloodshed.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Mufassal summarises the Quran; memorise it as a realistic goal and read its first cluster as a sequence of life choices.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The rivers of Paradise against the boiling water of Hell make the choice obvious.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: The Prophet's teachings only bring benefit; Islam is hard only the way studying is hard for a child.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Tribal partisanship ignores justice; help an oppressing relative by restraining him.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Stay principled however unprincipled the other side; never answer bigotry with bigotry.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Islam on the tongue versus internalised iman that directs behaviour, without judging anyone else's iman.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death's stupor is certain and we are soon forgotten, so stop clinging to what is not ours.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Avoid major sins and Allah's forgiveness covers the small slips.

quran.point: Assumption of jahiliyyah about Allah: the theological use of the word.
Display of jahiliyyah: the behavioural use.
Judgment of jahiliyyah: the political use.
Allah made iman beloved and beautified it in the believers' hearts.

hadith.gist: Help your brother whether he is oppressor or oppressed; you help the oppressor by holding him back from his oppression.
Heraclius questioned Abu Sufyan about the Prophet and, told that no one left the faith after entering it, said that is how iman is once its delight mixes with the heart.

maxims: Death comes after you; you spend life running from it
Islam is only as hard as studying is for a child
What you know is right but do not do is superficial
It was never acceptable to be wrong because the other side is
Stay away from the big stuff

stories.who: Hudaybiyyah: Quraysh barring the unarmed Muslims from umrah
stories.point: Their tribal zeal contrasted with the believers' serenity and restraint.
Submission comes first; iman must still enter the heart.
Those who taste the joy of iman do not leave it.

stories.who: An uncle's death in his childhood
stories.point: We avoid thinking of death because it takes away the fun.

contemporary: Muslims feeling constantly pressed to defend the Quran's verses on combat
Racist treatment that devalues a group's lives and opinions, and the temptation to reciprocate
takeaways: Measure your deeds against the Prophet's teaching so they count
Set a realistic memorisation goal, such as the last four juz, and work at it steadily
Hold your ethical ground and never answer bigotry or oppression in kind
Work to turn what you profess into values that shape your behaviour, without judging anyone else's iman
Remember death regularly, avoid the major sins and trust Allah's forgiveness for small slips

Oszc482Z-mk.speaker: adnan
Oszc482Z-mk.speaker_note: opens and closes both reminders with his usual formulas and continues his own nightly walk through the movements of the prayer from earlier nights of Ramadan 2024
Oszc482Z-mk.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 26: Sixth Night of Tahajjud
Oszc482Z-mk.one_line: Continuing the movements of the prayer: rising from ruku to praise Allah, the companion Rabi'ah's nights with the Prophet, and prostration as gratitude and dua.
Oszc482Z-mk.summary: Both reminders continue his walk through the movements of the prayer. After recalling that the standing is where we carry Allah's word back to Him as the Prophet recited it, he turns to rising from ruku and saying our Lord, to You is praise. When life is hard we choose between turning to Allah resentful, blaming the sky, or praising Him, and there is always a reason to praise; Dawud was told he had thanked Allah once he admitted that even his thanks was a blessing. The young companion Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b, who stayed near the Prophet at night to serve him, heard him recite, glorify and then repeat his praise, and when invited to ask for anything he asked for the Prophet's company in Paradise and was told to help by prostrating much. Praise is said standing tall because it displays the blessing you carry. The second reminder adds that the Quran is recited only standing, for its dignity; bowing acknowledges the gap between Creator and creation; ruku is for glorifying and sujud for dua. Placing the face on the ground is the only fitting thanks for a gift beyond comprehension, never given to a human, and the two prostrations are two chances to ask.

outline.heading: Interlude
The standing: carrying His word back to Him
outline.gist: Recalling the earlier movements, the standing is about the value of Allah's word, which we learn, memorise and recite back to Him in the form the Prophet recited, and long standing is a mark of dedication.

outline.heading: Praise even when struggling
outline.gist: When you are struggling you choose between turning to Allah resentfully and blaming the sky, or looking at yourself and praising Him.

outline.heading: The Prophet's words on rising from ruku
outline.gist: Our Lord, to You is praise filling the heavens and the earth; none can withhold what You give or give what You withhold.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b's night beside the Prophet
outline.gist: A teenage companion who loved the Prophet stayed near him at night to serve him, and between dozing he heard him recite, glorify in ruku and then repeat his praise after rising.

outline.heading: Dawud: even my praise is Your blessing
outline.gist: There is always a reason to praise Allah; Dawud asked how he could thank Him when his thanks was itself a blessing, and was told that now he had thanked Him.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah asks for the Prophet's company in Paradise
outline.gist: Invited to ask for anything, Rabi'ah rejected asking for something worldly like marriage and asked for the Prophet's company in Paradise; he was told to help by prostrating much.

outline.heading: Praise him standing tall
outline.gist: You say the praise standing straight, not bent low, because praise displays the blessing your Lord has given you.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reciting His word only while standing
outline.gist: The Quran is recited standing and not in other postures, because that dignified position suits His word.

outline.heading: Bowing to His station, rising to show His blessing
outline.gist: Bowing is less about respect than accepting the difference in station between you and Allah; rising, you praise Him in a way that reflects the blessings He has given.

outline.heading: Ruku for glorifying, sujud for dua
outline.gist: The Prophet said to exalt the Lord in ruku and strive in dua in sujud, for it is likely to be answered.

outline.heading: Prostration as the only fitting thanks
outline.gist: Putting the dignified body on the ground is the only way to show gratitude for a gift beyond comprehension; we grew up with it, but someone prostrating for the first time feels how meaningful it is, and it is never given to a human.

outline.heading: Two prostrations, two chances to ask
outline.gist: Sujud is where you make dua, and the second prostration gives you another chance to go back down and ask again.

outline.heading: Interlude

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: The standing and the rising from ruku, with the Prophet's words of praise, as movements with their own meaning.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Each movement in turn: reciting standing, bowing, rising to praise, and prostrating to glorify and ask.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Choose praise over resentment in hardship; even the ability to thank Allah is His blessing.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Prostration is the only way to express thanks for what Allah has given.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Bowing and prostrating acknowledge the gap between Creator and creation and are given to no human.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b's devotion to the Prophet and his request for his company in Paradise.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Sujud is the place of dua, and the two prostrations are two chances to ask.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Allah's word is recited only in the dignified standing position.

hadith.gist: The best prayer is the one with the longest standing.

On rising from ruku the Prophet said: Our Lord, to You is praise, abundant, good and blessed, filling the heavens and the earth and whatever You will beyond; none can withhold what You give or give what You withhold.
Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b, staying near the Prophet at night, woke to hear him recite the Fatihah, glorify his Lord in ruku and repeat 'to You is praise' after rising.
The Prophet told Rabi'ah to ask for anything; he asked for his company in Paradise, and the Prophet said: then help me against yourself with much prostration.
As for ruku, exalt the Lord in it; as for sujud, strive in dua in it, for it is fitting that you be answered.

maxims: Bowing accepts the difference in station
Two prostrations, two chances to ask
There is always a reason to praise

stories.point: A young companion who gave his nights to serving the Prophet and heard the praise in every posture of his prayer.
Admitting that even the ability to thank is a blessing from Allah is itself thanks.
He turned away from asking for something worldly and asked for the Prophet's company in Paradise, reached through much prostration.

takeaways: Say 'our Lord, to You is praise' standing upright, as a declaration of the blessings you have been given.
In hardship choose to praise Allah rather than resent Him, since there is always a reason to praise.
Prostrate often and use each sujud to ask, treating the second prostration as another chance.
Recite the Quran in the standing with the dignity owed to Allah's word.
Ask Allah for the highest things, such as the Prophet's company in Paradise, not only for worldly needs.

35:29.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتۡلُونَ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ سِرࣰّ ا وَعَلَانِيَةࣰ يَرۡجُونَ تِجَٰرَةࣰ لَّن تَبُورَ
35:29.en: Lo! those who read the Scripture of Allah, and establish worship, and spend of that which We have bestowed on them secretly and openly, they look forward to imperishable gain

35:30.ar: لِيُوَفِّيَهُمۡ أُجُورَهُمۡ وَيَزِيدَهُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ غَفُورࣱ شَكُورࣱ‏
35:30.en: That He will pay them their wages and increase them of His grace. Lo! He is Forgiving, Responsive

35:34.ar: وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَذۡهَبَ عَنَّا ٱلۡحَزَنَۖ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورࣱ شَكُورٌ
35:34.en: And they say: Praise be to Allah Who hath put grief away from us. Lo! Our Lord is Forgiving, Bountiful

64:17.ar: إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا يُضَٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
64:17.en: If ye lend unto Allah a goodly loan, He will double it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Responsive, Clement

42:23.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ ٱللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِۗ قُل لَّآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًا إِلَّا ٱلۡمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰۗ وَمَن يَقۡتَرِفۡ حَسَنَةࣰ نَّزِدۡ لَهُۥ فِيهَا حُسۡنًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ شَكُورٌ
42:23.en: This it is which Allah announceth unto His bondmen who believe and do good works. Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I ask of you no fee therefor, save lovingkindness among kinsfolk. And whoso scoreth a good deed We add unto its good for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Responsive

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah. It is therefore no sin for him who is on pilgrimage to the House (of Allah) or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord, (for him) lo! Allah is Responsive, Aware

4:147.ar: مَّا يَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمۡ إِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ وَءَامَنتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاكِرًا عَلِيمࣰ ا
4:147.en: What concern hath Allah for your punishment if ye are thankful (for His mercies) and believe (in Him)? Allah was ever Responsive, Aware

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

U_Fw_4EUTgE.speaker: adnan
U_Fw_4EUTgE.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice
U_Fw_4EUTgE.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Ash-Shakur (The Appreciative)
U_Fw_4EUTgE.one_line: Ash-Shakur, who rewards small deeds immensely, and how to live it through gratitude in action, thanking people, and sincere deeds.
U_Fw_4EUTgE.summary: Opening the names of tenderness, he defines Ash-Shakur as the One who answers small good deeds with enormous reward. He tells a run of narrations: the man who watered a thirsty dog, the woman of ill repute who did the same, the man who moved a thorny branch from a path, and Abu Sufyan, whose two small acts of decency before Islam, defending Fatimah against Abu Jahl and stopping the beating of a man smuggling food to the boycotted Muslims, he links to his later guidance. Charity is raised like a foal, and fasting is rewarded by Allah personally. He then reads the name through its Quranic pairings: with the Forgiving, because Allah first removes the flaws in our deeds then multiplies what remains; with the Forbearing, because there is no deadline; with the Knowing, because nothing goes unnoticed. Al-Hamid is praised by nature while Ash-Shakur is how He treats us, and only this name makes Paradise make sense, since our obedience benefits us alone. He gives three applications: turn praise into gratitude shown in behaviour by serving others, thank people and remember their favours as the Prophet always did while forgetting your own, and bring sincerity and enthusiasm to deeds that Allah multiplies so generously.

outline.heading: Meaning of Ash-Shakur and Ash-Shakir
outline.gist: The One who shows great appreciation and gives the greatest reward for small deeds.

outline.heading: The man who watered a thirsty dog
outline.gist: He filled his shoe from a well for a dog licking moist sand, and Allah appreciated it and forgave him.

outline.heading: Reward in every living soul; the woman who watered an animal
outline.gist: Every moist liver carries reward, and a woman who sold herself was forgiven for watering a thirsty animal.

outline.heading: Removing a thorny branch from the path
outline.gist: A man moved it so it would not harm Muslims, and Allah forgave him and admitted him to Paradise.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan defends Fatimah against Abu Jahl
outline.gist: When Abu Jahl slapped Fatimah, the non-Muslim Abu Sufyan had her slap him back, and the Prophet asked Allah to keep this for Abu Sufyan.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan stops the beating of an aid smuggler
outline.gist: During the boycott he defended a man feeding the starving Muslims; these two small deeds are linked to his later guidance.

outline.heading: Honour the elderly and you will be honoured
outline.gist: Whoever helps someone because of their age, Allah sends someone to help him in old age.

outline.heading: Charity raised like a foal
outline.gist: Allah accepts charity from good earnings with His right hand and grows it as one raises a young horse.

outline.heading: Fasting is Mine and I reward it
outline.gist: Only Allah and the servant know whether one truly fasted, so He rewards it personally.

outline.heading: A transaction that never loses
outline.gist: Those who recite the Book, pray and give receive their due and more from His bounty.

outline.heading: Paired with Al-Ghafur: flaws forgiven, the rest multiplied
outline.gist: Our deeds are imperfect, so He first forgives their flaws then appreciates what remains; the people of Paradise praise Him as Forgiving and Appreciative.

outline.heading: Paired with Al-Halim: no deadline
outline.gist: Whenever you finally do good, even late, He multiplies it and adds excellence to it.

outline.heading: Paired with Al-'Alim: nothing goes unnoticed
outline.gist: Any voluntary good is known to Him; and what would Allah gain from punishing you if you are grateful and believe.

outline.heading: Al-Hamid and Ash-Shakur: a two-way road
outline.gist: He is praiseworthy by nature; hamd is what He receives from you and shukr is how He treats you.

outline.heading: Only Ash-Shakur explains Paradise
outline.gist: Our deeds cannot affect Allah and only benefit us, yet He rewards them with eternity; it is hard to know this name and not love Him.

outline.heading: Living the name 1: from praise to gratitude in action
outline.gist: Hamd is the mental acknowledgement that begins the Quran and marks the Prophet; shukr is proving it through behaviour.

outline.heading: Few of My servants are grateful
outline.gist: Alhamdulillah rolls off the tongue, but shukr means using what you are given to serve others; be among the few.

outline.heading: Living the name 2: thank people as the Prophet did
outline.gist: He who does not thank people does not thank Allah; the Prophet never forgot a kindness done to him and never mentioned his own.

outline.heading: Living the name 3: be sincere and eager
outline.gist: If Allah forgives the flaws in your deed and multiplies it many times, it is rude to offer it reluctantly and without sincerity.

outline.heading: Outro

19:96.en: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love

5:54.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرۡتَدَّ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ يُحِبُّهُمۡ وَيُحِبُّونَهُۥٓ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ يُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوۡمَةَ لَآئِمࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
5:54.en: O ye who believe! Whoso of you becometh a renegade from his religion, (know that in his stead) Allah will bring a people whom He loveth and who love Him, humble toward believers, stern toward disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and fearing not the blame of any blamer. Such is the grace of Allah which He giveth unto whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

9:24.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ وَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ وَأَزۡوَٰجُكُمۡ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلٌ ٱقۡتَرَفۡتُمُوهَا وَتِجَٰرَةࣱ تَخۡشَوۡنَ كَسَادَهَا وَمَسَٰكِنُ تَرۡضَوۡنَهَآ أَحَبَّ إِلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَجِهَادࣲ فِي سَبِيلِهِۦ فَتَرَبَّصُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
9:24.en: Say: If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your wives, and your tribe, and the wealth ye have acquired, and merchandise for which ye fear that there will no sale, and dwellings ye desire are dearer to you than Allah and His messenger and striving in His way: then wait till Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

3:31.ar: قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
3:31.en: Say, (O Muhammad, to mankind): If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ

28:85.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لَرَآدُّكَ إِلَىٰ مَعَادࣲۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَمَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
28:85.en: Lo! He Who hath given thee the Qur'an for a law will surely bring thee home again. Say: My Lord is Best Aware of him who bringeth guidance and him who is in error manifest

3:139.en: Faint not nor grieve, for ye will overcome them if ye are (indeed) believers
