3:35.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ عِمۡرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطۡنِي مُحَرَّرࣰ ا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
3:35.en: (Remember) when the wife of 'Imran said: My Lord! I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated (offering). Accept it from me. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower

3:36.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتۡهَا قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعۡتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتۡ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلۡأُنثَىٰۖ وَإِنِّي سَمَّيۡتُهَا مَرۡيَمَ وَإِنِّيٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
3:36.en: And when she was delivered she said: My Lord! Lo! I am delivered of a female - Allah knew best of what she was delivered - the male is not as the female; and lo! I have named her Mary, and lo! I crave Thy protection for her and for her offspring from Satan the outcast

21:83.ar: ۞وَأَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
21:83.en: And Job, when he cried unto his Lord, (saying): Lo! adversity afflicteth me, and Thou art Most Merciful of all who show mercy

12:86.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُواْ بَثِّي وَحُزۡنِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
12:86.en: He said: I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah, and I know from Allah that which ye know not

12:83.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلٌۖ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأۡتِيَنِي بِهِمۡ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
12:83.en: (And when they came unto their father and had spoken thus to him) he said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience! It may be that Allah will bring them all unto me. Lo! He, only He, is the Knower, the Wise

f_XArNKxvYk.speaker: adnan
f_XArNKxvYk.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice; mentions his Damascus background
f_XArNKxvYk.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Wadud (The Most Loving)
f_XArNKxvYk.one_line: Al-Wadud, whose love wants nothing in return, shown through the Quran, the Prophet's life and Paradise, and how to love Him back.
f_XArNKxvYk.summary: He presents Al-Wadud, named only twice in the Quran, as love that expects nothing back. The Arabs ranked love in many degrees, and wudd is the pure kind, which is why Allah calls Himself Al-Wadud rather than a name implying He gains from being loved. Unlike faiths that imagine a lonely God who created for His own need, Islam holds that our love and obedience only fill our own hearts. He traces Allah's love through the hadith of the servant drawing near through voluntary deeds until heaven and earth love him, the first revelation beginning with Jibril's embrace, verses consoling the Prophet when he left Makkah, after Uhud and when revelation paused, and the beauty of the world itself. He describes intimate conversation with Allah as a level above asking, seen in the mother of Maryam, Ayyub, Ya'qub and the Prophet at Ta'if, and tells at length the story of the last man to leave Hell, who receives ten times the greatest kingdom, while the highest in Paradise wait only to see Allah again. To live the name: move from worship out of obligation to worship out of love, even in hardship; never forget that Allah already loves you; and love Allah, His Prophet, the believers and Islam to taste the sweetness of faith.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Wadud in Shu'ayb's call and Surat al-Buruj
outline.gist: Seek forgiveness, for He is Merciful and Loving; and after the brutal story of the trench of fire, He is the Forgiving, the Loving.

outline.heading: Why Al-Wadud and not Al-Habib
outline.gist: Loving is an acceptable description of Allah, but He named Himself Al-Wadud.

outline.heading: Wudd: the highest, purest love
outline.gist: The Arabs listed seventeen or eighteen degrees of love; wudd is love that wants nothing in return.

outline.heading: He gains nothing from our love
outline.gist: Other faiths imagine God created out of need or loneliness; Allah's status does not change, and loving Him only fills our hearts.

outline.heading: Degrees of Allah's love
outline.gist: There is a basic love for all creation and higher degrees earned by what you do.

outline.heading: Drawing near until He loves you
outline.gist: Through voluntary deeds the servant earns His love; Jibril and the dwellers of heaven are told to love him and acceptance is placed for him on earth.

outline.heading: If you love someone, tell them
outline.gist: The Prophet told a man who loved another to go and tell him.

outline.heading: Better to be judged by Allah than by your parents
outline.gist: A scholar said he would choose Allah's judgment because Allah is more compassionate than his parents.

outline.heading: Love prepared for the believers
outline.gist: The Most Merciful will appoint love for those who believe and do good, almost as a tangible gift awaiting them.

outline.heading: Revelation began with a hug
outline.gist: Jibril's first act was a tight embrace: serious and intimidating, but the whole story starts with love.

outline.heading: People He loves and who love Him
outline.gist: If some turn back, Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him; love runs throughout the Quran.

outline.heading: Love Allah above the eight beloved things
outline.gist: Believers love Allah most; parents, children, spouses, tribe, homes, wealth and trade must not outrank Him, and following the Prophet proves love.

outline.heading: The beauty of the world is His love
outline.gist: Al-Badi' made the world beautiful, and Al-Wadud is why He chose to make it so.

outline.heading: 'You are in Our eyes'
outline.gist: Like the Damascene phrase of keeping someone in your eyes, Allah tells the Prophet He watches over him lovingly.

outline.heading: Leaving Makkah heartbroken: He will bring you back
outline.gist: The Prophet wept leaving the land he loved most, and Allah promised his return.

outline.heading: After Uhud: do not grieve
outline.gist: Allah consoled the companions that they remain uppermost if they believe.

outline.heading: When revelation paused: your Lord has not forsaken you
outline.gist: After months without revelation and Quraysh's mockery, Allah swore by the morning light that He had not abandoned him.

outline.heading: Munajat: speaking to Allah beyond asking
outline.gist: Beyond dua is intimate conversation where you are not asking for anything.

outline.heading: The mother of Maryam talks to her Lord
outline.gist: She tells Allah she delivered a girl though He knew, and names her Maryam; this happens only where there is love.

outline.heading: Dua is the first level; the Prophet's conversations
outline.gist: Graduate from requests to placing your affairs in His hands; many of the Prophet's supplications are simply praise and conversation.

outline.heading: Ayyub: harm has touched me
outline.gist: His plea contains no request at all.

outline.heading: Ya'qub takes his grief to Allah
outline.gist: Losing his sight from grief, he complained only to Allah and did not even ask.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dua at Ta'if
outline.gist: After being abused he complained to Allah of his weakness, coming from a place of love.

outline.heading: If those who turn away knew My longing
outline.gist: Allah's love for those who leave Him would melt their hearts; how then does He love those who come to Him.

outline.heading: Labbayk: the Prophet's first talbiyah
outline.gist: On his first umrah the companions heard him chant labbayk, an eager response of a heart that wants to please Him.

outline.heading: The last man to leave Hell
outline.gist: He promises again and again to ask for nothing more, Allah keeps giving, and finally grants him ten times the greatest king's dominion in Paradise.

outline.heading: The highest people: gazing at His face
outline.gist: They see Allah twice a day and wait only for the next time; nothing else matters to them.

outline.heading: Living the name 1: love Him back
outline.gist: He has already given more than you can repay; worship out of obligation is a starting point, but move to doing things out of love, even amid pain and loss.

outline.heading: Living the name 2: acknowledge He loves you
outline.gist: There is easy love and tough love; nothing that happens can cancel the love He has already shown.

outline.heading: Living the name 3: love people and taste faith's sweetness
outline.gist: Love Allah and His Prophet most, love people for Allah's sake, and hate leaving Islam as you would hate the fire.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dua for Allah's love
outline.gist: He asked for Allah's love, the love of those who love Him, and of deeds that bring one closer to His love.

vfkNCqEUhrQ.title: Freedom, Jihad and Knowledge (Reduced Concepts, Episode 3)
vfkNCqEUhrQ.one_line: How freedom shrank to the right to mock, jihad to combat, and knowledge to a framed degree, and how to recover each concept.
vfkNCqEUhrQ.summary: He takes three broader concepts. Freedom, the cornerstone of Western civilization, has been reduced to the right to offend and mock while the range of acceptable opinion is quietly narrowed, as Chomsky described; cancel culture, the demand to condemn Hamas before speaking about Gaza, and taboo topics show that tyranny exists here in prettier packaging. A value with exceptions is not a value. Individual liberty must be limited by harm, including indirect and long-term harm, as COVID showed. Islam forbids even inner contempt, yet Muslims should welcome critique of their faith rather than riot over cartoons, because an idea that fears critique is weak and Allah's word is stronger. Tawhid frees a Muslim from every line not drawn by Allah, so Muslims should champion liberty. Jihad, used 41 times in the Quran and called the pinnacle of Islam, means striving; reducing it to combat, which few Muslims ever face, loses a mindset that turns all of life into worship and expects difficulty, so people expect much of themselves and little of others. Knowledge has been reduced to a degree: he values self-study, oral explanation over exams, useful skills such as time, money and sleep management, the human sciences and trades, and above all mentorship, citing his Quran programme in Syria that raised school retention dramatically.

outline.heading: Opening
General concepts, and intentions that need renewing
outline.gist: Today's concepts are not specifically Islamic but model the method; like intentions, values lose their substance and must be renewed.

outline.heading: Liberty, the cornerstone of the West, has lost substance
outline.gist: Western civilization was built on liberty, and unless it is renewed Western societies will suffer.

outline.heading: Freedom reduced to offending the sacred
outline.gist: Is free speech now just the right to say hurtful things and disrespect what others hold holy, and to ignore the collective's wellbeing?

outline.heading: Chomsky: limit the spectrum, allow lively debate
outline.gist: The smart way to control people is to restrict the range of acceptable opinion while encouraging debate within it until the limits feel sacred.

outline.heading: Open repression versus a wider spectrum
outline.gist: Middle Eastern regimes simply forbid thought; the West does the same with more finesse, and a value with exceptions is not a value.

outline.heading: One forbidden topic means no liberty
outline.gist: Being barred from one subject is as problematic as being barred from all; the harm just shows later.

outline.heading: The Prophet's struggle was for the freedom to speak
outline.gist: He only asked to explain his message freely; Islam has no room for coercion, and Quraysh denied people the liberty to accept it.

outline.heading: Free to curse politicians, not everything
outline.gist: Criticising leaders is refreshing for immigrants, but some topics carry consequences, as the joke about cursing the other country's leader shows.

outline.heading: Where individual liberty ends: do no harm
outline.gist: Individual liberty now trumps everything, though every society rests on the rule of not harming oneself or others.

outline.heading: Ignoring indirect and long-term harm
outline.gist: Liberty is limited only by direct harm, while actions that harm others indirectly or years later are barely considered.

outline.heading: Hate speech versus free speech
outline.gist: Distinguishing them is a thin line that requires intelligence and reflection.

outline.heading: Islam forbids even inner contempt
outline.gist: Tazkiyah teaches that harbouring contempt for others is arrogance and bad assumption, let alone voicing it.

outline.heading: Critiquing an idea is not racism
outline.gist: Attacking Islam as an idea is legitimate and welcome because Muslims can answer it; stereotyping Muslims as people is different.

outline.heading: Mockery is not critique
outline.gist: One may point out what is wrong with a figure or religion but mocking the sacred is not an academic form of free speech.

outline.heading: The cartoons: mockery achieves nothing
outline.gist: The 2006 caricatures of the Prophet only hurt and marginalised, persuading no one.

outline.heading: The Muslim response was worse
outline.gist: Claiming no one may speak about Islam is wrong; others have that right, and since our idea is from Allah we should invite the debate.

outline.heading: Muslims restricting critique of their own history
outline.gist: Branding people deviant for saying historical figures erred limits thought and repels people.

outline.heading: An idea afraid of critique is weak; tyranny in prettier packaging
outline.gist: Nothing in Islam fears scrutiny; tyranny in the West is as real as in the Middle East, just better wrapped.

outline.heading: Cancel culture as a smear instead of a cell
outline.gist: Stepping outside acceptable opinion costs jobs, relationships and reputation, which is arguably worse than prison.

outline.heading: Gaza and the 'do you condemn Hamas' test
outline.gist: Those speaking about civilian deaths in Gaza were asked to condemn first, a trap to place them outside acceptable opinion.

outline.heading: One bad opinion cancels every argument
outline.gist: If science worked this way, one bad paper would erase a scientist's good work; the argument itself no longer matters.

outline.heading: Liberty reduced to satire and obscenity
outline.gist: We accepted freedom as late-night mockery, protest and posting anything, while losing the ability to speak our minds on certain topics.

outline.heading: No communal protection for dissenting views
outline.gist: When a controversial university poster appeared, no one could speak without ruin; on topics like gender identity logic no longer matters.

outline.heading: Taboo even in health policy
outline.gist: Suggesting a two-tier health system gets one labelled far right regardless of the argument.

outline.heading: Islam came to a free people
outline.gist: The Arabs, never conquered and free in mind even when enslaved, were chosen for the message because one cannot carry Islam without freedom.

outline.heading: Tawhid frees you from others' red lines
outline.gist: Only Allah draws the lines, so a Muslim questions laws, stands against oppression, and is not enslaved by wealth, power or fear.

outline.heading: Muslims should champion liberty
outline.gist: Viewing Western freedom as 'too much' is a mistake; restricting liberty costs people the ability to practise Islam with integrity.

outline.heading: COVID: liberty and indirect harm
outline.gist: One person's free choice of meal shut down the planet, showing behaviour must be weighed for indirect, long-term harm.

outline.heading: 'My body, my life' and the collective
outline.gist: Reducing liberty to doing whatever one wants ignores how dress and conduct between genders affect society.

outline.heading: Jihad: a word we were taught to whisper
outline.gist: Jihad, striving, appears 41 times in the Quran, an unusually high frequency for a value, yet Muslims are ashamed to say it.

outline.heading: The pinnacle of Islam, confused with combat
outline.gist: The Prophet called jihad the peak of the matter; combat came only after permission to fight in Madinah, which many companions did not want.

outline.heading: Jihad before arms, and its many categories
outline.gist: The word was used in Makkah when fighting was not permitted; scholars list around fourteen kinds, with combat the last.

outline.heading: An umbrella over all of life
outline.gist: Work, family and self-purification all become striving for Allah, keeping a person in constant mujahadah and turning life into worship.

outline.heading: Why combat is emphasised: the ultimate sacrifice
outline.gist: Few Muslims ever bore arms; the Quran highlights it because willingness to give one's life proves willingness to give everything less.

outline.heading: Expectations shape how we live
outline.gist: The same clinic day feels bad or good depending on what he expected; high expectations of others bring constant disappointment.

outline.heading: Jihad as a mindset that expects difficulty
outline.gist: Expecting challenges makes calm days a pleasant surprise and prepares a person to function when hardship comes.

outline.heading: Expect little from others, much from yourself
outline.gist: That is how he keeps friends and survives dawah work, and it makes a person more productive.

outline.heading: Knowledge reduced to a degree on the wall
outline.gist: One of his most learned teachers never attended school yet knew Alfiyyat Ibn Malik by heart.

outline.heading: University gives tools; learning is on you
outline.gist: Proficiency comes from the personal reading and work done after the degree.

outline.heading: The oral tradition versus exams
outline.gist: Students once proved understanding by explaining a text to the teacher; exams assess almost nothing.

outline.heading: Useless information clutters the mind
outline.gist: Should knowledge be applicable? Much of what we absorb from phones serves no purpose.

outline.heading: Learning cut off from mentorship
outline.gist: Knowledge must come with guidance on character, humility and service, which is why the ministry is named for upbringing before education.

outline.heading: His Quran programme in a Syrian village
outline.gist: With 350 students in a village of 3,000, he collected school report cards and held children accountable, while some parents did not even know they attended.

outline.heading: Mentorship raised school retention
outline.gist: Investing in each child took grade-ten retention from about 11 percent to 47 percent within two years.

outline.heading: Life skills are knowledge too
outline.gist: Presenting yourself, managing money, time and sleep, and social skills matter more than arithmetic.

outline.heading: Human sciences and trades deserve respect
outline.gist: Communities push every child into medicine or engineering and look down on political science, media, arts and trades, and suffer for it.

outline.heading: Lifelong learning and al-Qarawiyyin
outline.gist: Muslims must learn all their lives; the first university, founded by Fatima al-Fihri in the ninth century, granted degrees in medicine and Shariah.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Mentorship transforms outcomes; communities should value human sciences and trades.

53:31.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَى
53:31.en: And unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, that He may reward those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good with goodness

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

wBD1rFbc0ag.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 24: Fourth Night of Tahajjud
wBD1rFbc0ag.one_line: Two short reminders: Allah's vast forgiveness for those who avoid the major sins, and praising and asking Him for good in both worlds.
wBD1rFbc0ag.summary: The first reminder draws on the verses of An-Najm recited later in the night: Allah repays those who do evil for what they did and those who do good with the best, and those who keep away from the major sins and indecencies, apart from small slips, will find their Lord vast in forgiveness. The point is that the believer's effort goes into avoiding the great sins while trusting Allah's forgiveness for the lapses that every person falls into. The second reminder begins with the words of praise to Allah, abundant, good and blessed, as our Lord loves and is pleased with, then turns to what to ask Allah for, touching on the grave and this life, and closes with the Quranic dua for good in this world, good in the hereafter and protection from the Fire.

60:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ يُبَايِعۡنَكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّا يُشۡرِكۡنَ بِٱللَّهِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَسۡرِقۡنَ وَلَا يَزۡنِينَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلۡنَ أَوۡلَٰدَهُنَّ وَلَا يَأۡتِينَ بِبُهۡتَٰنࣲ يَفۡتَرِينَهُۥ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِنَّ وَأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ وَلَا يَعۡصِينَكَ فِي مَعۡرُوفࣲ فَبَايِعۡهُنَّ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُنَّ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:12.en: O Prophet! If believing women come unto thee, taking oath of allegiance unto thee that they will ascribe no thing as partner unto Allah, and will neither steal nor commit adultery nor kill their children, nor produce any lie that they have devised between their hands and feet, nor disobey thee in what is right, then accept their allegiance and ask Allah to forgive them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

11:25.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
11:25.en: And We sent Noah unto his folk (and he said): Lo! I am a plain warner unto you

11:26.ar: أَن لَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
11:26.en: That ye serve none, save Allah. Lo! I fear for you the retribution of a painful Day

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: The chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved, said: We see thee but a mortal like us, and we see not that any follow thee save the most abject among us, without reflection. We behold in you no merit above us - nay, we deem you liars

11:28.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَءَاتَىٰنِي رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِهِۦ فَعُمِّيَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنُلۡزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمۡ لَهَا كَٰرِهُونَ
11:28.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you, if I rely on a clear proof from my Lord and there hath come unto me a mercy from His presence, and it hath been made obscure to you, can we compel you to accept it when ye are averse thereto

11:29.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
11:29.en: And O my people! I ask of you no wealth therefor. My reward is the concern only of Allah, and I am not going to thrust away those who believe - Lo! they have to meet their Lord! - but I see you a folk that are ignorant

11:30.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ مَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِن طَرَدتُّهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
11:30.en: And, O my people! who would deliver me from Allah if I thrust them away? Will ye not then reflect

11:31.ar: وَلَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمۡ عِندِي خَزَآئِنُ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ وَلَآ أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكࣱ وَلَآ أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزۡدَرِيٓ أَعۡيُنُكُمۡ لَن يُؤۡتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ خَيۡرًاۖ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:31.en: I say not unto you: "I have the treasures of Allah" nor "I have knowledge of the Unseen," nor say I: "Lo! I am an angel!" Nor say I unto those whom your eyes scorn that Allah will not give them good - Allah knoweth best what is in their hearts - Lo! then indeed I should be of the wrong-doers

11:33.en: He said: Only Allah will bring it upon you if He will, and ye can by no means escape

11:34.ar: وَلَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ نُصۡحِيٓ إِنۡ أَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَنصَحَ لَكُمۡ إِن كَانَ ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يُغۡوِيَكُمۡۚ هُوَ رَبُّكُمۡ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
11:34.en: My counsel will not profit you if I were minded to advise you, if Allah's will is to keep you astray. He is your Lord and unto Him ye will be brought back

YoKPdxWyQT4.title: Islam, Tawheed and Following the Prophet (Reduced Concepts, Episode 2)
YoKPdxWyQT4.one_line: How Islam, tawhid and following the Prophet have been reduced to rituals, a phrase and outward appearance, and what each concept really means.
YoKPdxWyQT4.summary: Continuing the series, he applies the idea of reduced concepts to three core terms. First, Islam: translating deen as religion, a set of rituals to a deity, loses its meaning of what we owe Allah in principles and conduct. The companions' pledges and the questions of the Day of Judgment go far beyond rituals. Islam is a worldview with reform at its heart, refusing oppression, as Surah Hud shows through seven prophets each confronting a different corruption; a domesticated, purely spiritual Islam serves dictators and explains the ruin of the Muslim heartlands. It is practised outside the masjid, which is only a training ground, and the hypocrisy of religious people is a leading reason people leave Islam. Every teaching has a purpose, so parents must give children real reasons. Second, tawhid is not merely a phrase but the single, all-knowing source of ethical red lines, which is why it frees people and why values stay constant, unlike man-made lines that keep shifting. He distinguishes fixed ethics from fiqh, where difference is normal, and mocks those who fight over moon sighting while lying openly. Third, following the Prophet means thinking and treating people as he did, not only dressing like him; the Sunnah is his way, shown in his gentleness with the Bedouin in the masjid. He asks people to keep the outward forms but prioritise the values.

outline.heading: Opening
Values before rulings: the Makkan surahs
outline.gist: Recapping episode one, he notes the Prophet spent thirteen years building principles, and Makkan surahs are value-driven with no legal rulings.

outline.heading: Mushaf order and revelation order
outline.gist: The difference between the order of the book and the order of revelation gives each verse extra dimensions of meaning.

outline.heading: Three concepts for today
outline.gist: He will examine Islam, tawhid and following the Prophet, modelling a method people can apply to other values themselves.

outline.heading: Islam is not 'religion' in the dictionary sense
outline.gist: Dictionary definitions reduce religion to acts of worship for a superhuman being, which is not what deen means.

outline.heading: Language as a source of reduction
outline.gist: Even Arabic speakers now assign different meanings to words than they carried when the Quran and Prophet used them.

outline.heading: Deen: what you owe Allah
outline.gist: Deen shares a root with debt; it is the principles, ethics and behaviours one owes Allah.

outline.heading: The five pillars are not all of Islam
outline.gist: The hadith of Jibril divides the deen into islam, iman and ihsan; limiting it to rituals implies no other obligations exist.

outline.heading: The companions' pledges went beyond rituals
outline.gist: Pledges to give sincere counsel to every Muslim, never to fall but standing, and not to contest leadership without clear cause show the deen's scope.

outline.heading: The questions of the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: We will be asked about our time, wealth, conduct and youth, none of them rituals.

outline.heading: Islam as a worldview and way of life
outline.gist: Islam is the method of serving Allah on earth and touches every detail of life.

outline.heading: Reform is Islam's edge
outline.gist: Remove reform from any ideology and it becomes toothless, which is what those who want the status quo prefer.

outline.heading: Companions content with their own community
outline.gist: Some companions did not want to engage beyond Madinah, but the Prophet taught them Badr was about righteousness, not wealth, and that Islam refuses oppression.

outline.heading: Dictatorships want a quiet Islam
outline.gist: Tyrants are happy for Muslims to practise as long as they never challenge corruption or nepotism.

outline.heading: Surah Hud: seven prophets, seven corruptions
outline.gist: Nuh faced class prejudice, others faced arrogance, entitlement and economic corruption, and Ibrahim faced isolation; each brought a different reform.

outline.heading: A purely spiritual Islam does not work
outline.gist: Reducing Islam to a personal spiritual connection leaves something missing even for someone without heavy trials.

outline.heading: A domesticated Islam and the ruined heartlands
outline.gist: Islam turned timid and quiet, and Palestine, Sham, Iraq, Egypt, Libya and Tunisia, once its centres, are now shells mirroring our hollow values.

outline.heading: Islam is practised outside these walls
outline.gist: People come to the masjid to gain strength to practise Islam outside it.

outline.heading: Hospitals, workplaces, schools and streets
outline.gist: Islam governs our dealings with everyone; the idea that it lives only in the masjid was pushed politically and many have accepted it.

outline.heading: Religious hypocrisy drives people away
outline.gist: A survey of Western Muslims found the conduct of visibly religious people was the top reason for leaving Islam.

outline.heading: What 'praying in the first row' really means
outline.gist: The reward is for arriving early enough to earn the spot, not for blocking in other cars or pushing through rows to get there.

outline.heading: The masjid as a training ground
outline.gist: If the masjid bans all interaction between men and women, it fails to train people to interact respectfully outside, where they must.

outline.heading: Every teaching has a purpose
outline.gist: Allah's laws aim at benefits for the individual and community; teaching purposeless obedience damages the mind.

outline.heading: Growth for its own sake is cancer
outline.gist: As an oncologist he compares purposeless growth to cancer cells; even dawah must have a purpose beyond numbers.

outline.heading: Give children real reasons
outline.gist: Reduced concepts start at home; a meaningless answer either drives a child away or dulls his critical thinking.

outline.heading: Tawhid: the one unforgivable matter
outline.gist: Islam in one word is tawhid, yet it has been reduced to a phrase; why is shirk the one thing Allah will not forgive?

outline.heading: Belief without consequence: the purple planet
outline.gist: If tawhid were only a belief with no effect, like belief in a purple planet, its importance would make no sense.

outline.heading: The red lines concept
outline.gist: Every life has red lines such as murder, theft, lying and adultery; tawhid concerns who draws them.

outline.heading: Who draws the lines?
outline.gist: The West decided lines were drawn by fallible humans, for control, in another time, and so may be redrawn.

outline.heading: How man-made lines shift
outline.gist: Comparing 1920s photographs to today shows how lines are pushed a little each year when their source is not sacred.

outline.heading: Tawhid means one source of ethics
outline.gist: Lines drawn by the all-knowing, all-wise Allah are sacred, so a Muslim dropped into any time or place behaves the same.

outline.heading: A constant source gives constant values
outline.gist: Multiple variable sources yield variable ethics and constant searching for exceptions.

outline.heading: Ethics are not fiqh
outline.gist: Jurisprudential questions like fasting while ill allow differing opinions; ethics and values are a different category.

outline.heading: Fighting over moon sighting while lying openly
outline.gist: People battle over Ramadan calculations and masjid design yet lie to their families; he personally likes moon sighting but it is legitimately disputed.

outline.heading: We cannot differ on honesty
outline.gist: Teaching children to say you are not home teaches them to lie; a believer's values are carved in rock, not drawn in sand.

outline.heading: Tawhid frees people from other masters
outline.gist: Taking direction from a sacred source makes a person a threat to the powerful, who rename vices like alcohol to normalise them.

outline.heading: Shaytan moves the line a millimetre a year
outline.gist: Without a fixed source, values slowly fall until new forbidden things seem normal; tawhid keeps us from lying, stealing, harming and oppressing.

outline.heading: Flexible rulings, fixed lines
outline.gist: Muslims may seek easier fiqh, such as fasting when the sun barely sets, but no one touches the lines Allah drew.

outline.heading: Following the Prophet: the goal is to resemble him
outline.gist: Drawing on his earlier series on intellectual followship, he asks what resembling the Prophet actually means.

outline.heading: Appearance is the easy part
outline.gist: Anyone with money can buy a turban and robe and be treated as holy.

outline.heading: The respirator he wears to keep his beard
outline.gist: He goes through yearly fit-testing for a powered respirator rather than shave, showing he values outward sunnah.

outline.heading: Think the way he thought
outline.gist: He is not belittling appearance; the bulk of following him is processing the world as he did.

outline.heading: Dimensions of his intellect
outline.gist: His planning, broad vision, logic, methodological empathy and civilizational perspective were the subjects of his earlier series.

outline.heading: Sunnah means his way
outline.gist: In the Quran sunnah means a way; emulating anyone starts with their values and conduct, not their socks.

outline.heading: A mystic or a man of wisdom?
outline.gist: Reducing the Sunnah to recommended extras hides the Prophet's intellect and philosophy and makes youth feel they cannot relate to him.

outline.heading: The Sunnah of holding the door
outline.gist: Entering with the right foot means nothing if you push others aside; his way is serving people, as his own teachers did.

outline.heading: The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid
outline.gist: The Prophet let him finish, then gently explained what the masjid is for, and the man learned his deen.

outline.heading: Open hearts that bring people a step closer
outline.gist: His Sunnah is people who love Allah and help others along, even one step at a time.

outline.heading: From one prayer to zero, or to two
outline.gist: A man who prayed only one prayer was berated and stopped praying, until a wiser imam encouraged him to two.

outline.heading: The broken vase and the shisha cafe
outline.gist: A lost young man scolded for breaking something in a masjid found a warm welcome at a shisha cafe and never came back.

outline.heading: Taraweeh reduced to a number
outline.gist: Muslims have argued for centuries over eight or twenty rak'ahs instead of the substance and joy of the recitation.

outline.heading: Take it all, but prioritise the values
outline.gist: Keep the dhikr, the masjid and the outward sunnah, but give the bigger concepts equal attention, as the companions followed him in everything before the details.

outline.heading: Outro

And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion

Y1U1ez1QfII.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 25: Fifth Night of Tahajjud
Y1U1ez1QfII.one_line: A sound heart that stays steady, making the hereafter one's concern, and the danger of the world opening up to us.
Y1U1ez1QfII.summary: The first reminder takes Ibrahim's dua in Ash-Shu'ara not to be disgraced on the Day when wealth and children are of no use, only a sound heart. A sound heart is not a spiritual high that rises for a time and then drops again. The Prophet said that whoever makes the hereafter his concern, Allah places richness in his heart, gathers his affairs and the world comes to him humbled, while whoever makes the world his concern has poverty set before his eyes and his affairs scattered, getting only what was written for him. The second reminder recalls the Prophet's words when wealth arrived with Abu Ubaydah: it is not poverty he feared for his followers but the world being spread before them so that they compete for it and are destroyed as earlier nations were. Many who were once guided have been ruined this way, and Allah describes this life as play, adornment, boasting and rivalry in wealth and children. The remedy is perspective: whoever wakes safe at home, healthy, with food for the day, has been given the whole world.

outline.heading: A sound heart, not a passing spiritual high
outline.gist: Ibrahim asked not to be disgraced on the Day when only a sound heart benefits; such a heart is steady, not a spiritual high that comes for a while and drops away.

outline.heading: Make the hereafter your concern
outline.gist: Whoever is concerned with the hereafter is given richness of heart, gathered affairs and a world that comes to him humbled; whoever is concerned with the world has poverty before his eyes and scattered affairs.

outline.heading: Ruined by the world after guidance
outline.gist: Many who were once guided have been destroyed by worldly rivalry, which Allah describes as play, amusement, adornment, boasting and competing in wealth and children.

outline.heading: Safe, healthy and fed: the whole world is yours
outline.gist: Whoever wakes secure at home, healthy in body and with food for the day has been given the world entire, so the heart should see what it already has.

outline.heading: Interlude

koiHXDCdaH0.speaker: adnan
koiHXDCdaH0.speaker_note: his annual Ramadan series; says he runs the masjid, is a physician and grew up in Syria
koiHXDCdaH0.title: Moral Collapse and State Failure (Reduced Concepts, Episode 1)
koiHXDCdaH0.one_line: Introducing Reduced Concepts: civilizations fall when their founding values shrink to empty rituals, and Muslims recover by restoring what those concepts meant.
koiHXDCdaH0.summary: He opens his Ramadan series with a thesis from the Iraqi writer Ahmed Khairi al-Omari: every civilizational collapse is preceded by a reduction of the values that built it. Muslims, he argues, are there now, with Islam reduced to ritual, ethics to an empty smile and knowledge to a certificate, which is why prayer no longer restrains people from wrongdoing as the Quran says it should. To show this is a recognised pattern, he surveys theories of societal collapse: direct causes such as climate, war and disease versus underlying causes, chiefly cognitive decline. He draws on Toynbee's stages and responses to decline (archaism, futurism, detachment, transcendence), which he links to the hadith of renewal; Quigley on institutions that start serving themselves, which he applies to Muslim charities with institutional ego; Sorokin's cycles of principles; Spengler's loss of figurative thinking; Diamond's attitudes to change, illustrated by resistance to children in the masjid; and Ibn Khaldun on how declining societies breed superstition and pointless argument. The goal is to recover the substance behind concepts like the caliphate, unity and protection rather than copy their old forms, especially for the youth. Citing Malek Bennabi, he ends that a society's wealth lies in its ideas, and that Islam triumphed through the strength of its idea.

outline.heading: Opening
The thesis: civilizations fall after their concepts are reduced
outline.gist: Quoting an Iraqi writer, he argues Muslim values have been reduced to skeletons: Islam to rituals, ethics to a fake smile, knowledge to a certificate.

outline.heading: Prayer that no longer prevents wrongdoing
outline.gist: People pray for decades without the effect the Quran promises because the concept of salah has been emptied to its mechanics.

outline.heading: The aim: learning to think and trace our steps back
outline.gist: The series is not meant to make people feel bad but to help them recognise reduced concepts in their own lives and correct them.

outline.heading: Moral collapse and state failure: values become rituals
outline.gist: From Blanton's paper: collapse is preceded by values shrinking into superficial rituals, meaningless practices or corrupt ideas; the series will analyse Islamic concepts this way.

outline.heading: Climate as a historical cause of collapse
outline.gist: Past climate shifts toppled societies; today humans are driving the change, and outside the Western bubble survival is getting harder.

outline.heading: Direct causes: disaster, war, economy, disease
outline.gist: Direct causes are tipping points that expose a society that had already fallen.

outline.heading: Underlying causes: cognitive decline
outline.gist: Scholars agree loss of thinking and creativity underlies collapse, and he argues reduced values explain the Muslim world's lack of unity, justice and education.

outline.heading: Energy return on investment
outline.gist: A society consuming more energy than it produces heads toward collapse; clean energy does not yet meet our needs.

outline.heading: Toynbee: civilizations decline from within
outline.gist: Toynbee's stages of genesis, growth, troubles, universal state and disintegration, with collapse driven mainly by internal factors.

outline.heading: The powerful few and the excluded many
outline.gist: Disintegrating societies split into a ruling minority and the rest; practising Muslims are outside the circles of power, which is dangerous.

outline.heading: Archaism: idealising the past
outline.gist: Declining societies believe everything was better before; personal nostalgia that drives self-accountability is healthy, but a society worshipping its past is a sign of collapse.

outline.heading: Futurism: escaping into the future
outline.gist: Others idealise a technological future while poverty and addiction persist in the West as much as elsewhere.

outline.heading: Detachment: withdrawing from the community
outline.gist: Some Muslims step back from a dysfunctional community, and it is hard to convince them to return and improve it.

outline.heading: Transcendence and the renewer of each century
outline.gist: Toynbee's search for new insight parallels the hadith that Allah sends a renewer every hundred years to clear the dust from the deen without changing it.

outline.heading: Quigley: institutions that serve themselves
outline.gist: Social instruments turning into institutions that put their own survival above the needs they were built for is a hallmark of decline.

outline.heading: Institutional ego in Muslim organisations
outline.gist: A charity is only a means to serve the community and has no innate value; when people channel their egos into it, survival becomes the goal and it must change.

outline.heading: Sorokin: cycles of principles
outline.gist: Civilizations rise and fall as principles are upheld then neglected; Muslims need not replace theirs, only return to their authentic versions.

outline.heading: What we can do: recognise symptoms and work backwards
outline.gist: Without political power, Muslims can still start by asking what a concept like salah meant then versus now and restoring it.

outline.heading: Spengler: the winter of a civilization
outline.gist: Civilizations move in seasons and can return to spring; in winter, abstract thinking fades.

outline.heading: Losing figurative thinking leads to copy-paste religion
outline.gist: Without the ability to draw parallels, values from one context are copied literally into another and lose their substance; renewal means showing what they mean today.

outline.heading: Youth who see Islamic concepts as empty
outline.gist: It hurts that young people hear terms like taqwa as meaningless phrases because they have never seen anyone benefit from them.

outline.heading: The civilizational leap of the first generations
outline.gist: Within about fifty years Arabia went from illiteracy to a three-continent civilization of scholars and scientists, built on powerful values we have lost the ability to translate.

outline.heading: Jared Diamond and attitudes toward change
outline.gist: Among five causes of collapse, an inability to accept the need to change is one Muslims especially struggle with.

outline.heading: Children in the masjid: resistance to change
outline.gist: When he started a Quran programme, elders complained about noise and even threw children's shoes in the dumpster; welcome them with sweets instead or lose them for good.

outline.heading: Treating yourself as the golden standard
outline.gist: People object weekly that the masjid is not run as back home, such as having no curtain; assuming your habits are Islam's standard is arrogance.

outline.heading: Ibn Khaldun, the father of sociology
outline.gist: His Muqaddimah founded the study of collective human behaviour, governance and values, yet Muslims have neglected it compared with Western scholars.

outline.heading: Oppression corrupts ethics and breeds argument
outline.gist: Ibn Khaldun noted that declining, unfree societies lose their ethics and fill with superstition, rumour and opportunists; the yearly fight over paying zakat al-fitr in cash is an example.

outline.heading: Restoring values is the way back
outline.gist: If Muslims correct their concepts and reclaim the narrative of what Islam is and how to practise it, the ummah can recover.

outline.heading: The caliphate: recover the concept, not the form
outline.gist: Trying to recreate the old model exactly is archaism; what we need is what it stood for: representation, leadership, unity and protection.

outline.heading: Gaza and the absence of protection
outline.gist: The killing of some 34,000 people in Gaza, documented live by people on the ground, would not have happened if any shred of protection remained.

outline.heading: Successor and Commander of the Believers
outline.gist: The titles of early leaders show the role was stewardship and responsibility for people's wellbeing.

outline.heading: A series aimed at the youth
outline.gist: Statistically someone in the room will hold office one day; if they fix their concepts now they can address the bigger picture later.

outline.heading: An ummah thirsty for unity
outline.gist: Morocco's World Cup semi-final run sparked joy everywhere, showing how thirsty Muslims are for any togetherness.

outline.heading: Start with understanding the concepts
outline.gist: Explain jihad, zakat, chastity and other terms properly; youth are passionate and truthful and will lead if they see the light in a concept.

outline.heading: Malek Bennabi: a society's wealth is its ideas
outline.gist: His favourite modern Muslim thinker held that a society is rich by its ideas, not its possessions.

outline.heading: Why the indebted United States still leads
outline.gist: Despite huge debt the US attracts the minds; as an oncologist he waits for guidelines from American centres, and money without ideas means nothing.

outline.heading: Islam prevailed through the strength of its idea
outline.gist: With no river, no state, no literacy, no army and no wealth, the Prophet won because Quraysh could not defeat the Quran's idea.

outline.heading: Stronger ideas prevail; we welcome debate
outline.gist: A strong idea wins if its carriers persevere; Muslims need not fear debate because their idea is from Allah, but they must study the concepts that built the nation.

outline.heading: Outro

K-BgN8qwbwY.title: The Rituals (Reduced Concepts, Episode 4)
K-BgN8qwbwY.one_line: Prayer, fasting, Hajj, dhikr, dua and khushu as fuel and meaning rather than mechanics, and the danger of giving up on growth.
K-BgN8qwbwY.summary: Calling this the core of the series, he first warns that the real danger is making peace with reduced concepts: a person who keeps striving, however far behind, is better than one far ahead who has stopped, as Imam Ahmad's 'not yet' on his deathbed shows. He then asks whether rituals are a burden or fuel. Salah has been reduced to mechanics that fiqh can validate but that leave youth cold; it is meant as a privileged check-in with the King, a connection, and a way of taking a stand, sustained by love rather than discipline, as the Prophet's joy in prayer shows. Practical steps include pausing one's train of thought and centring the intention before praying. Fasting teaches need versus want, reveals untapped potential, builds compassion, and is not a licence to feast at night; the first Ramadan held Badr. Hajj is not walking around rocks but retracing Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family and the Prophet; Hajar's useless-seeming running teaches us to do our best, and Hajj should be done young. Dhikr must engage mind and heart: alhamdulillah builds optimism and gratitude, subhanallah turns blame inward, and istighfar drives daily improvement and humility. Dua is a conversation, not Aladdin's lamp, and khushu is an emotional response to agreeing with Allah's commands, not tears.

outline.heading: The main course: our rituals
outline.gist: This episode is the heart of the series: the ritual and Islamic concepts the companions received that changed how they lived and thought.

outline.heading: What did these concepts do for them?
outline.gist: We admire the companions' lives but feel unable to emulate them, so we stay in the box we put ourselves in.

outline.heading: The real danger is accepting the reduction
outline.gist: We have made peace with values that no longer function; as long as you have not given up, there is hope.

outline.heading: The striver behind beats the one who stopped
outline.gist: Someone ten steps behind who is still trying is better with Allah than someone far ahead who has stopped holding himself accountable.

outline.heading: The higher you are, the harder the fall
outline.gist: Stopping means falling from a greater height, so the only choice is continued self-awareness and striving.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad: 'not yet'
outline.gist: On his deathbed he refused Iblis's suggestion that he had made it; Shaytan gives the illusion of arrival to make us stop.

outline.heading: Rituals: fuel or burden?
outline.gist: Most of us experience rituals as an inconvenience in our day, which is the core problem.

outline.heading: Night prayer before a heavy message
outline.gist: The earliest revelations ordered long night prayer because a heavy message was coming; changing words is not enough, we must change how we think.

outline.heading: Salah as the tray that holds every deed
outline.gist: His teacher compared prayer to a serving tray: the bigger your prayer, the more of your other good deeds it can carry.

outline.heading: Mechanics are necessary but not the whole
outline.gist: Without the mechanics prayer is invalid, but a jurist can only rule on the mechanics, not on the connection.

outline.heading: The hundred-metre sprint prayer
outline.gist: In many places prayer has become rapid up-and-down movement with no essence.

outline.heading: Why youth disengage from prayer
outline.gist: A rational mind sees no value in mechanical movements five times a day; prayer is meant to hold us back from sin.

outline.heading: A privilege: checking in with the King
outline.gist: Prayer is the chance to speak to the King of kings five times a day about your fears and hopes; refusing it is beyond rude.

outline.heading: Allah faces the one who prays
outline.gist: Allah turns toward the servant in prayer and asks, when he is distracted, whether he has found something better.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah exists to improve prayer
outline.gist: Nearly every practice of spiritual training aims at making prayer meaningful and bringing peace.

outline.heading: The man told to pray again
outline.gist: The Prophet sent him back three times and then taught him to pray with stillness in each position.

outline.heading: Hit the brakes before you pray
outline.gist: He writes down his train of thought before prayer, then centres himself; that is what intention really is.

outline.heading: Salah means connection
outline.gist: The word means connection, as in the command to pray for the believers; a prayer with no connection is an empty concept.

outline.heading: Establishing prayer means taking a stand
outline.gist: To establish prayer means to take a stand for what you believe and the direction of your life.

outline.heading: Love, not discipline, sustains it
outline.gist: The Prophet's long night prayers and scholars' full recitations came from love; discipline got him through the Quran in one night only once.

outline.heading: Speaking to God five times a day
outline.gist: Explain it to a non-Muslim friend and you sound like the most spiritual person in the room, yet we do not feel it.

outline.heading: The Prophet's joy in prayer and Abu Bakr's tears
outline.gist: Prayer was his rest and the coolness of his eyes; he insisted Abu Bakr, who wept through his recitation, lead the prayer, preserving an example of its depth.

outline.heading: Provoking your own analysis
outline.gist: The aim is for people to examine whether their own values are full or shrivelled and make changes themselves.

outline.heading: Fasting: need versus want
outline.gist: Fasting fills over eight percent of life and teaches the difference between needing and wanting, which the ego blurs.

outline.heading: Clarity when food and desire are removed
outline.gist: Without food and intimacy distracting us, spirituality rises and we get more done.

outline.heading: The inner voice and the first day after Ramadan
outline.gist: A hushed inner voice re-emerges; after Ramadan his workday feels easy and he is more patient than colleagues.

outline.heading: Potential: the question is will you
outline.gist: Ramadan proves you can do more; manage time, hold yourself accountable and raise expectations of yourself.

outline.heading: Eating less and learning compassion
outline.gist: Eating less is healthier, as the Prophet and philosophers taught, and hunger builds empathy for those who suffer.

outline.heading: Not a licence to feast at night
outline.gist: Ramadan is not packing the day's food into one meal or becoming irritable; keep fasting voluntarily afterwards.

outline.heading: The first Ramadan held Badr
outline.gist: In the very first Ramadan the companions fasted in the desert heat and fought the battle that established the Muslim community, the Day of Distinction.

outline.heading: Against the odds, then the last ten nights
outline.gist: Outnumbered three to one with almost no cavalry, they won and returned for the final nights of Ramadan.

outline.heading: Hajj reduced to rocks
outline.gist: Taken literally, Hajj is walking around and between rocks and throwing pebbles; the word means setting out for a destination you value above all hardship.

outline.heading: Pilgrims who did not know why they came
outline.gist: Living in Makkah as a child he saw most pilgrims knew only that Hajj wipes sins, not that rights owed to people remain.

outline.heading: Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina: Adam and Hawwa
outline.gist: The rites retrace humanity's parents reuniting, forgiving one another and planning how to win back what they lost.

outline.heading: Tawaf: harmony with the universe
outline.gist: Everything from electrons to galaxies circles counterclockwise; tawaf is a prayer, requiring wudu, joining that motion.

outline.heading: Sa'i: rewarded for what you strive toward
outline.gist: Allah rewards what you work toward, not only what you achieve, like someone memorising a line a day who dies with three pages.

outline.heading: Hajar's running: do your best
outline.gist: Her running between the hills changed nothing materially, yet she gave all she had, and Allah brought out Zamzam.

outline.heading: Three layers of the Hajj
outline.gist: Each step echoes Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family, and the Prophet's thoroughly documented Hajj; experience any of them.

outline.heading: The value is the symbolism, not the place
outline.gist: Makkah's landscape has nothing to see; without absorbing the meaning, Hajj becomes rushed mechanics and a status title.

outline.heading: Go to Hajj young
outline.gist: Hajj is physical walking and standing; go after university or early marriage rather than in old age, ideally before children.

outline.heading: Conceptual remembrance
outline.gist: Counted dhikr is essential; his teachers said thousands daily out of sheer joy in saying Allah's name.

outline.heading: Engage the mind and heart, not only the tongue
outline.gist: Begin with the words, then grow into understanding what praise, glorification and tawhid mean.

outline.heading: Alhamdulillah forces optimism
outline.gist: Praising Allah requires finding the good in any situation.

outline.heading: The scholar who lost a leg and a son
outline.gist: On one journey he lost his leg and a son, and praised Allah for leaving him more than He took.

outline.heading: Why Muslims keep rebuilding
outline.gist: The attitude of alhamdulillah is why Muslims, including in Gaza, rebuild and never lose hope.

outline.heading: Gratitude and wellbeing
outline.gist: Psychology shows grateful people live longer and better; focusing on the one missing thing is not living.

outline.heading: Subhanallah turns blame inward
outline.gist: Declaring Allah flawless means asking what I could do about suffering rather than blaming God, and it brings acceptance and sincerity.

outline.heading: Istighfar builds a nation
outline.gist: Sincerely acknowledging a mistake each day means improving each day, which is why the Quran ties seeking forgiveness to rain and flourishing.

outline.heading: Istighfar and humility
outline.gist: Focusing on your own sins leaves no room to feel superior to others.

outline.heading: Dua is not Aladdin's lamp
outline.gist: Dua is an ongoing conversation; Allah answers by granting now, later, something better, or averting harm.

outline.heading: Ramadan is designed for dua
outline.gist: Use Ramadan to build the habit of taking your hopes and fears to Allah all year.

outline.heading: Khushu: an emotional response to agreement
outline.gist: His definition: an emotional response to mentally agreeing with and accepting Allah's commands, like going to the pharmacy at night grudgingly or gladly.

outline.heading: Try it in prayer; it is not tears
outline.gist: Stand in prayer grateful to be exactly where you should be; reducing khushu to crying misses the point, and not everyone can cry.

outline.heading: Outro

39:71.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَيُنذِرُونَكُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَاۚ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ

But the word of doom of disbelievers is fulfilled

39:72.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
39:72.en: It is said (unto them): Enter ye the gates of hell to dwell therein. Thus hapless is the journey's end of the scorners

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: And those who keep their duty to their Lord are driven unto the Garden in troops till, when they reach it, and the gates thereof are opened, and the warders thereof say unto them: Peace be unto you! Ye are good, so enter ye (the Garden of delight), to dwell therein

40:28.ar: وَقَالَ رَجُلࣱ مُّؤۡمِنࣱ مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَكۡتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقۡتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبࣰ ا فَعَلَيۡهِ كَذِبُهُۥۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقࣰ ا يُصِبۡكُم بَعۡضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡرِفࣱ كَذَّابࣱ‏
40:28.en: And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah, and hath brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then his lie is upon him; and if he is truthful, then some of that wherewith he threateneth you will strike you. Lo! Allah guideth not one who is a prodigal, a liar

40:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ سُلۡطَٰنٍ أَتَىٰهُمۡ إِن فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ إِلَّا كِبۡرࣱ مَّا هُم بِبَٰلِغِيهِۚ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
40:56.en: Lo! those who wrangle concerning the revelations of Allah without a warrant having come unto them, there is naught else in their breasts save pride which they will never attain. So take thou refuge in Allah. Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

42:15.ar: فَلِذَٰلِكَ فَٱدۡعُۖ وَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۖ وَقُلۡ ءَامَنتُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن كِتَٰبࣲۖ وَأُمِرۡتُ لِأَعۡدِلَ بَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمۡۖ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡۖ لَا حُجَّةَ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
42:15.en: Unto this, then, summon (O Muhammad). And be thou upright as thou art commanded, and follow not their lusts, but say: I believe in whatever scripture Allah hath sent down, and I am commanded to be just among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. Unto us our works and unto you your works; no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and unto Him is the journeying

42:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمۡرُهُمۡ شُورَىٰ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
42:38.en: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them

3:159.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.en: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him)

nCZBT5koNlQ.speaker: adnan
nCZBT5koNlQ.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads; speaks as the imam about his teachers and his community
nCZBT5koNlQ.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 23: Quranic Reflections (Az-Zumar 62 to Ash-Shura 23)
nCZBT5koNlQ.one_line: The Ha-Mim surahs as a manual for dawah: connection with Allah, example, reference and consultation, plus free belief, advocacy, repelling evil with good and arrogance.
nCZBT5koNlQ.summary: He introduces the Ha-Mim surahs as a cluster on carrying Islam to other people, each giving advice on what to do and what to avoid. Ghafir pairs taking the message to those who argue with constant dua, since you cannot call people to a God you do not know; Fussilat shows that dawah through conduct works better than words; Ash-Shura requires a reference and a community run by consultation. He presses that Muslim communities and institutions in the West rarely consult their people or one another, citing the Prophet's habit of withholding his view and following the majority before Uhud. From the end of az-Zumar he teaches that no one walks to Paradise alone, so choose your group, and contrasts the closed and open gates of Hell and Paradise. The believer from Pharaoh's family leads him to freedom of belief, the persecution of speech through cancellation, the narrowing range of acceptable opinion since October 7, the difference between Zionism and Judaism, and the need for communities to organise and back those who speak instead of demanding courage from imams alone. He closes with repelling evil with excellence, a verse balancing conviction with tolerance, and arrogance as the root of rejecting truth.

outline.heading: Opening
The Ha-Mim cluster: carrying dawah to individuals
outline.gist: From Ghafir to al-Ahqaf the surahs share an opening, the story of Musa and paired positive and negative advice on carrying Islam to other individuals, unlike the earlier cluster about carrying the message as a nation-building way of life.

outline.heading: Ghafir: take dawah to those who argue, while making dua
outline.gist: Bring the message to those who oppose it and, in parallel, keep a personal connection with Allah; calling people to a God you do not know is counterproductive.

outline.heading: Fussilat: dawah through behaviour works better
outline.gist: Those who keep refusing spoken dawah are held to account, while dawah through conduct forces no one to listen and has more impact.

outline.heading: Ash-Shura: dawah needs a reference
outline.gist: Without a body of knowledge to refer people to you either look lost or make up answers that cause harm.

outline.heading: Shura as consultation: your voice matters
outline.gist: Consultation is the closest Islamic idea to democracy: even if you are not the leader you have a say in decisions that affect the group, as the Prophet taught and the surah describes.

outline.heading: Without consultation the dawah goes nowhere
outline.gist: These three surahs give positive advice and the next three warn of pitfalls; if everyone works alone in silos with no consultation, the message will not be carried far.

outline.heading: Community decisions cannot be made by a few
outline.gist: Muslim minorities in the West do this poorly: big decisions about money, direction and priorities need broad input, and no imam or institution may steer the community without coordinating with others.

outline.heading: The Prophet held back his view: leaving Madinah for Uhud
outline.gist: He asked for advice and kept his own opinion to himself so as not to sway people; outvoted, he put on his armour and refused to reverse the decision, and after the loss he was told to keep consulting.

outline.heading: Do Muslim institutions even try?
outline.gist: He doubts institutions across the city and North America care about the views of their congregations or of neighbouring institutions.

outline.heading: Consultation is not for rulings
outline.gist: Legal rulings belong to those who spent years studying; consultation covers direction, resources and priorities.

outline.heading: Listening to needs: the community survey
outline.gist: The masjid's social innovation lab surveys people's needs, fears and struggles as a modern form of shura; what remains is institutions coordinating with each other.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sincerity is one to One, yet the surah is named for groups
outline.gist: Sincerity means pleasing no one but Allah in your heart, but it does not require living alone; the name az-Zumar points to groups.

outline.heading: No one walks to Jannah alone: choose your group
outline.gist: Believers and disbelievers are both driven in groups; find the people who will walk you to Paradise or a group of Hell will find you, since you rise with those you loved, meaning those you invested your time and care in.

outline.heading: Closed gates for Hell, open gates for Paradise
outline.gist: A host who opens the door before you arrive is hospitable; the people of Hell must knock at closed gates while the gates of Paradise open as its people approach. He tells of a friend who took seven minutes to answer his door.

outline.heading: Did no messengers come to you?
outline.gist: The keepers cannot understand how anyone who was warned could end up there; Allah did not make it hard to love or obey Him, so arriving there is shameful.

outline.heading: We heard but did not listen
outline.gist: The keepers assume some excuse, but the people admit they received the message and ignored it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The believer of Pharaoh's family
outline.gist: An example of dawah joined with connection to Allah: a man who concealed his faith for most of his life speaks up when they plan to kill Musa.

outline.heading: Concealing faith for a valid reason
outline.gist: Some people cannot practise openly for valid reasons, and Allah accepts from them.

outline.heading: Answering a thought with the sword is bankruptcy
outline.gist: Would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah? The verse is an argument for freedom of belief: meeting words with violence shows you have no better idea and no self-control.

outline.heading: Cancellation as persecution
outline.gist: Dictatorships make critics disappear; here people are cancelled, losing jobs and reputation, which he sees as no different, echoing the Arabic saying that cutting provision is like cutting off the head.

outline.heading: The shrinking range of acceptable opinion
outline.gist: Governments and other groups now limit what can be said in public; he has seen physicians sent through months of remediation for an overheard remark.

outline.heading: Since October 7: the condemnation trap
outline.gist: The constant demand that Muslims condemn was used to keep them from speaking about what was happening every day, and the space to speak against Zionism is still missing.

outline.heading: Zionism is an ideology, not Judaism
outline.gist: Muslims do not hate Jews, who are closest to them in faith, related by blood and have lived among Muslims for millennia; Zionism is a dangerous ideology that denies others the right to live in their ancestral lands.

outline.heading: Advocacy and organisation must change
outline.gist: For anything to change, the community's advocacy and organisation must grow so it has the pull to protect its people; he recalls being pressed to speak on the radio about a sensitive issue.

outline.heading: Clergy speak freely because institutions back them
outline.gist: Church clergy say far more aggressive things without being cancelled because their churches stand behind them, while an imam who misspeaks is left alone.

outline.heading: His teacher: stand up and I will answer
outline.gist: A teacher once refused an anonymous dangerous question unless the asker stood with him; people who demand public statements should share the risk or work communally to protect the speaker.

outline.heading: Brave with someone else's life
outline.gist: Demanding courage from imams while risking nothing is a toxic narrative; imams who challenge the status quo are routinely cut off, so support them first and push opinion out as a community effort.

outline.heading: If he lies, the lie is his burden
outline.gist: If the man is lying his lie will catch up with him, and if truthful you will be struck by what he warns of; this believer escaped alive, a rare happy ending, unlike the man in Ya-Sin.

outline.heading: Interlude
Good and evil are never equal: repel with the best
outline.gist: Answer the harm people do to you with the best you have, not merely with good; it is easy to say and borderline impossible to do.

outline.heading: Your enemy becomes a close friend
outline.gist: Most people who harm others are struggling or weak; met with excellence, nearly all calm down, reassess and seek friendship.

outline.heading: It takes grit and humility, and it works
outline.gist: It requires courage, sincerity and swallowing your ego; if you cannot articulate Islam, this is your dawah, and he testifies from experience that it works.

outline.heading: Interlude
His teacher's favourite verse: dawah in short commands
outline.gist: The verse is cut into small pieces, each one a way Muslims carry their dawah.

outline.heading: Call, stay upright, believe in every Book, be just
outline.gist: Keep calling and stay on the straight path, do not follow people's whims, believe in every revealed scripture, and treat others with justice and equality.

outline.heading: Our deeds and your deeds: Allah will judge
outline.gist: Each side lives by its conviction and argument may reach a dead end; the Muslim outlook combines identity and clarity with tolerance: I invite you, I will not persecute you, and Allah will judge between us.

outline.heading: Interlude
Arguing about Allah's signs without proof
outline.gist: Those who dispute Allah's signs and existence have no argument that can stand; the real cause lies in their chests.

outline.heading: Arrogance: acting from a status you do not have
outline.gist: Arrogance is believing yourself above where you are and treating people from there, such as looking down on religious people's flaws and rejecting their message; we are all equal.

outline.heading: Seek refuge from arrogance
outline.gist: Ask Allah's protection from ever looking down on others as ignorant, weak or unworthy of compassion; nothing worse can live in the heart.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The Ha-Mim surahs as a manual: dawah to opponents with dua, through behaviour, with a reference and consultation.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Shura means people have a say; institutions must consult congregations and coordinate with each other, as the Prophet did before Uhud.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: People are driven to Paradise and Hell in groups, met by open or closed gates.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Choose the group that will walk you to Paradise; you rise with those you invested your love in.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: The believer of Pharaoh's family argues for freedom of belief; cancellation and narrowing acceptable opinion are persecution too.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Since October 7 Muslims have been kept from speaking; Zionism is an ideology distinct from Judaism.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: Speaking publicly needs organised community backing, not demands that imams risk everything alone.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Repelling evil with the best you have turns enemies into friends and is itself dawah.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Conviction and justice side by side: invite, do not persecute, and leave judgment to Allah.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Arrogance underlies rejection of Allah's signs; seek refuge from looking down on anyone.

quran.point: Believers conduct their affairs by consultation among themselves.
After Uhud the Prophet was told to keep consulting his companions.

hadith.gist: The Prophet often asked his companions for their advice and followed the majority; before Uhud he kept his preference to stay in Madinah to himself, and once armoured refused to reverse the decision.
A person will be with those he loves on the Day of Judgment.
The Prophet will be the first to knock at the gate of Paradise and have it opened.

maxims: If you want people to know Allah, you should know Him too
Find your group, or a group of Jahannam will find you
Respond to words with a fist and you are bankrupt
Everyone is brave when it is someone else's life
Push back against evil with the best you have

stories.who: The Prophet and the consultation before Uhud
stories.point: He withheld his own view, followed the majority and kept consulting even after the loss.

stories.who: A friend who took seven minutes to open the door
stories.point: Making a guest wait at a closed door is inhospitable, which is how the people of Hell are received.
He defended Musa's right to believe and called his people with reason; he escaped alive.

stories.who: His teacher and the anonymous question
stories.point: Those who want dangerous things said must share the risk with the one who says them.
Ash-Shura 15 lays out the whole Muslim approach to dawah in short commands.

contemporary: Cancel culture and people losing jobs and reputations over speech
Physicians sent through months of remediation for overheard remarks
Pressure on Muslims to condemn after October 7 and limits on criticising Zionism
Muslim institutions in the city and across North America not consulting their communities or one another
The masjid's social innovation lab community needs survey
Church clergy backed by their institutions when they speak
Imams cut off by their institutions for challenging the status quo
takeaways: Pair calling others to Allah with your own dua and connection to Him
Let your behaviour carry the message, and refer questions to sound knowledge instead of improvising
Run community decisions on direction, money and priorities through real consultation
Choose companions who will walk you to Paradise
Repel harm with the best you have, and seek refuge from arrogance

42:47.ar: ٱسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِرَبِّكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلۡجَإࣲ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّكِيرࣲ‏
42:47.en: Answer the call of your Lord before there cometh unto you from Allah a Day which there is no averting. Ye have no refuge on that Day, nor have a ye any (power of) refusal

42:52.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ رُوحࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَمۡرِنَاۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدۡرِي مَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ وَلَا ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِن جَعَلۡنَٰهُ نُورࣰ ا نَّهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَاۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهۡدِيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
42:52.en: And thus have We inspired in thee (Muhammad) a Spirit of Our command. Thou knewest not what the Scripture was, nor what the Faith. But We have made it a light whereby We guide whom We will of Our bondmen. And lo! thou verily dost guide unto a right path

42:53.ar: صِرَٰطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ أَلَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
42:53.en: The path of Allah, unto Whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Do not all things reach Allah at last
