43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers flowing under me? Can ye not then discern

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable and can hardly make (his meaning) plain

43:53.ar: فَلَوۡلَآ أُلۡقِيَ عَلَيۡهِ أَسۡوِرَةࣱ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مُقۡتَرِنِينَ
43:53.en: Why, then, have armlets of gold not been set upon him, or angels sent along with him

43:54.ar: فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
43:54.en: Thus he persuaded his people to make light (of Moses), and they obeyed him. Lo! they were a wanton folk

43:67.ar: ٱلۡأَخِلَّآءُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:67.en: Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah)

44:38.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
44:38.en: And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in play

44:39.ar: مَا خَلَقۡنَٰهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
44:39.en: We created them not save with truth; but most of them know not

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهࣰ ا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهࣰ اۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
46:15.en: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee)

46:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنۡهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَعۡدَ ٱلصِّدۡقِ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ
46:16.en: Those are they from whom We accept the best of what they do, and overlook their evil deeds. (They are) among the owners of the Garden. This is the true promise which they were promised (in the world)

46:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ أُفࣲّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيٓ أَنۡ أُخۡرَجَ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلۡقُرُونُ مِن قَبۡلِي وَهُمَا يَسۡتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيۡلَكَ ءَامِنۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
46:17.en: And whoso saith unto his parents: Fie upon you both! Do ye threaten me that I shall be brought forth (again) when generations before me have passed away? And they twain cry unto Allah for help (and say): Woe unto thee! Believe! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. But he saith: This is naught save fables of the men of old

46:18.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فِيٓ أُمَمࣲ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
46:18.en: Such are those on whom the Word concerning nations of the jinn and mankind which have passed away before them hath effect. Lo! they are the losers

46:19.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ دَرَجَٰتࣱ مِّمَّا عَمِلُواْۖ وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
46:19.en: And for all there will be ranks from what they do, that He may pay them for their deeds; and they will not be wronged

46:21.ar: ۞وَٱذۡكُرۡ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذۡ أَنذَرَ قَوۡمَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَحۡقَافِ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦٓ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
46:21.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) of the brother of A'ad when he warned his folk among the wind-curved sandhills - and verily warners came and went before and after him - saying: Serve none but Allah. Lo! I fear for you the doom of a tremendous Day

46:29.ar: وَإِذۡ صَرَفۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ نَفَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنصِتُواْۖ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوۡاْ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
46:29.en: And when We inclined toward thee (Muhammad) certain of the jinn, who wished to hear the Qur'an and, when they were in its presence, said: Give ear! and, when it was finished, turned back to their people, warning

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright

28:34.ar: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفۡصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانࣰ ا فَأَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعِيَ رِدۡءࣰ ا يُصَدِّقُنِيٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
28:34.en: My brother Aaron is more eloquent than me in speech. Therefor send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Lo! I fear that they will give the lie to me

25:43.ar: أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيلًا
25:43.en: Hast thou seen him who chooseth for his god his own lust? Wouldst thou then be guardian over him

_c37Q1hcvB8.speaker: adnan
_c37Q1hcvB8.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads, continuing his own cluster framework from the previous night
_c37Q1hcvB8.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 24: Quranic Reflections (Ash-Shura 24 to the end of Al-Ahqaf)
_c37Q1hcvB8.one_line: The Ha-Mim warnings for those carrying dawah: materialism, delusion, arrogance in knowledge, and accepting that outcomes belong to Allah; plus friendship, mockery and responding to Allah now.
_c37Q1hcvB8.summary: He finishes the Ha-Mim cluster on carrying Islam to individuals. After recalling the three positive pieces of advice from Ghafir, Fussilat and Ash-Shura, he presents the three warnings: az-Zukhruf against judging by glitter and running religious life like a business, ad-Dukhan against delusional optimism that ignores the signs, and al-Jathiyah against arrogance born of knowledge. Al-Ahqaf closes by reminding that even perfect effort does not control who responds, as Hud's people refused while jinn listened unbidden. From Ash-Shura he urges responding to Allah now, as fully as you can rather than perfectly, while you can still repent, and describes the Quran as a spirit that gives life and a light that guides. Az-Zukhruf's verse on close friends becoming enemies leads to a long reflection on love for Allah's sake, which must be proven by helping each other toward Him, and on choosing companions as the most important decision of life. Pharaoh's mockery of Musa's speech shows the hollow logic of materialism and the danger of ridiculing what people cannot control. Ad-Dukhan reminds that creation is serious, and al-Jathiyah warns that a knowledgeable person can still make his desires his god. He ends by lifting the burden of judging where others will end up.

outline.heading: Opening
The Ha-Mim cluster: advice and warnings for dawah
outline.gist: Unlike the earlier cluster on establishing Islam as a civilisation, these seven surahs are operational advice on bringing individuals to Islam or to appreciating what they have.

outline.heading: Ghafir: take it to those who argue, while connected to Allah
outline.gist: Do not wait for people who ask; engage those who oppose, in parallel with your own dua.

outline.heading: Fussilat: dawah is best done through behaviour
outline.gist: Pushing words on people who refuse puts them in jeopardy, while achievements, character and ethics affect people more.

outline.heading: Ash-Shura: reference points and consultation
outline.gist: Have clear values to refer to and move as a community that has agreed on its direction.

outline.heading: Az-Zukhruf: the pitfall of materialism
outline.gist: Judging by what looks flashy rather than by substance, and running masjids and communities like businesses, will fail on the path of dawah.

outline.heading: Ad-Dukhan: delusional thinking and ignoring the signs
outline.gist: Telling yourself comforting lies and ignoring visible gaps dooms a community; this is why he keeps pointing out problems instead of indulging in blind optimism.

outline.heading: Al-Jathiyah: arrogance with knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran's profound values give Muslims insight, but if that knowledge leads to looking down on those without it or who refuse it, the decline is hard to recover from.

outline.heading: Al-Ahqaf: the outcome is in Allah's hands
outline.gist: Even if you follow every recommendation and avoid every warning, you cannot control who listens; sometimes the best job gets no response.

outline.heading: Hud's people refused; the jinn listened unbidden
outline.gist: Hud did everything right and was rejected, while jinn the Prophet never addressed heard and believed; the same uncertainty applies to raising your children.

outline.heading: Not bulletproof, but required
outline.gist: The surah ends the cluster to say the advice does not always work, yet it must be followed; dua keeps dawah from becoming I am right and you are wrong instead of wanting to share a blessing.

outline.heading: Musa did everything right
outline.gist: Each of these surahs carries Musa's story because he followed every recommendation and avoided every pitfall, and still did not get the response he hoped for.

outline.heading: Interlude
Respond to your Lord before the day with no return
outline.gist: Respond to His teachings, commands and recommendations now; once you stand before Him there is no going back to try again.

outline.heading: No refuge and no slap on the wrist
outline.gist: There is nowhere to hide that day and no lenient reproach; the judgment is final with no appeal, which sums up the whole surah.

outline.heading: Respond, not obey flawlessly
outline.gist: Allah asks us to respond, not to be perfect, because He acknowledges our deficits; as He answers our dua, we answer Him by prioritising His commands and trying our best.

outline.heading: Watch your own response, not others'
outline.gist: Each person's capacity differs, so spend less time judging how others follow and more on whether your own response is your best.

outline.heading: The priceless chance to fix things now
outline.gist: Right now you can repent and change immediately; that opportunity is priceless because it will soon be gone.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Quran as a spirit and a light
outline.gist: Allah describes the revelation as a spirit from His command, something alive that gives life, revealed to a Prophet who knew nothing of scripture.

outline.heading: Guiding to the straight path by the light you carry
outline.gist: People were dead inside and the Quran revived them; because the Prophet carries that beacon he guides to the path of Allah, to whom all matters return.

outline.heading: Close friends become enemies, except the God-conscious
outline.gist: On Judgment Day the closest friends will want nothing to do with each other unless they shared mindfulness of Allah.

outline.heading: Friends remind you of what you did together
outline.gist: That day you will see each friendship only by which side of the scale your time together falls on; time not spent helping each other toward Allah turns love into contempt.

outline.heading: Those who love for Allah on pulpits of light
outline.gist: Those who love one another for Allah's sake will stand on pulpits of light so honoured that prophets admire them.

outline.heading: What love for Allah's sake means
outline.gist: A friendship with no worldly calculation, built on each helping the other become closer to Allah and a better person.

outline.heading: Love needs proof
outline.gist: Love in Islam is not just a feeling; without encouraging each other to good and away from bad it is meaningless, while real love offers hope.

outline.heading: Hold on to friends who draw you closer
outline.gist: Such people are rare; an intimate relationship ends either as something envied or as enmity.

outline.heading: Choose your company more carefully than your car
outline.gist: Be picky about friends, the most important decision of your life; people spend months choosing a car but little thought on who surrounds them, which decides their Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pharaoh's case against Musa, told only here
outline.gist: Friendships built on material benefit fail, and az-Zukhruf alone records Pharaoh arguing why his people should follow him and not Musa.

outline.heading: Am I not better? Mocking Musa's speech
outline.gist: Pharaoh boasts of Egypt's rivers and sovereignty and belittles Musa as unprotected and unable to speak clearly; Musa knew his weakness and asked for Harun as a more eloquent partner.

outline.heading: The logic of materialism
outline.gist: Musa is beloved and revered, yet Pharaoh judges by strength, wealth and fluency and asks why he has no gold bracelets or escorting angels; none of it bears on the message.

outline.heading: He made fools of his people
outline.gist: Pharaoh treated his people as fools and they obeyed; the argument was hollow and offensive.

outline.heading: Beware of mocking what people cannot control
outline.gist: Mockery and satire are dangerous even among friends; ridiculing a trait someone did not choose is below the belt, and if people do it to you, do not sink to their level.

outline.heading: Attacking the person when you cannot beat the idea
outline.gist: Losing debaters dig up a bad photo or a past flaw to shift attention; Pharaoh, ruler of Egypt, feared Musa because a strong idea frightens power.

outline.heading: Interlude
Not created in play, but with truth
outline.gist: Within ad-Dukhan's warning against delusion, Allah says He did not create the heavens and earth in jest but with truth; existence is serious.

outline.heading: The Prophet joked, but never about serious things
outline.gist: Things prevail only through truth and crumble against it; take yourself lightly if you like, as the Prophet smiled and joked often, but know where the line is.

outline.heading: A book filled with play
outline.gist: Hold yourself to the standard of truth you will be judged by; a record of endless play with no commitment, grit or serious decisions will not end well.

outline.heading: Taking desire as one's god
outline.gist: Al-Jathiyah warns against arrogance with knowledge: have you seen the one who takes his whims as the one he worships?

outline.heading: Your god is whatever you obey without question
outline.gist: No religion literally worships desire, so this figure of speech shows how Allah defines worship: what you obey immediately and never question.

outline.heading: Actions prove whom you worship
outline.gist: When the scales of reason weigh a dilemma and the self always wins, desire is your god whatever you claim.

outline.heading: Misguided despite knowledge
outline.gist: Unlike the similar verse in al-Furqan, this one adds that he was led astray knowingly; knowledge that does not help you control urges and tell revelation from the self's selfishness has no value.

outline.heading: Knowledge without guidance, and the sealed heart
outline.gist: Such knowledge only breeds arrogance, vanity and envy, and increases distance from Allah; hearing, heart and sight are sealed.

outline.heading: Admit you are far and keep fighting
outline.gist: Acknowledging you are not doing well need not make you despair, but without it there is no fight against the self; even if you are losing, put up the fight.

outline.heading: Using knowledge to serve the self
outline.gist: Once you defend whatever you want as right, you use knowledgeable arguments to serve hidden struggles for power and position while sealed off from insight.

outline.heading: Interlude
The dutiful child and the defiant one
outline.gist: Al-Ahqaf contrasts the person kind to his parents and children who loves Allah, whose good is accepted and bad forgiven, with the one who rebukes his parents and rejects Allah.

outline.heading: Degrees for everyone, and no one wronged
outline.gist: Each group receives ranks according to what it did and no one is treated unjustly; you control neither who believes nor who is rewarded.

outline.heading: A burden lifted
outline.gist: Where others end up is not your business; follow the recommendations, heed the warnings and leave the rest to Allah.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The Ha-Mim surahs as three recommendations and three warnings for carrying Islam to individuals.

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects
themes.note: Materialistic judgment by appearance and treating religious work like business.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Delusional optimism that ignores the community's real gaps.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Do everything right and still leave results to Allah, as Hud and Musa did.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Respond to Allah as fully as you can, not flawlessly, and attend to your own response.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: The present chance to repent and change is priceless because it ends.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran as a life-giving spirit and a guiding light.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Friendships turn to enmity unless built on helping each other toward Allah; choosing company is life's most important decision.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Mocking traits people cannot control, and attacking the person instead of the idea.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Creation is serious and made with truth; a life of endless play fails that standard.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Knowledge without guidance breeds arrogance and lets desire become one's god.

themes.label: Withholding judgment of others
themes.note: Where people end up is Allah's business, not ours.

quran.point: Hud warned his people at al-Ahqaf and they refused despite his doing everything right.
A group of jinn listened to the Quran without the Prophet addressing them.
Allah answers the caller, so let people respond to Him.
Musa asked for Harun because he was more eloquent.
The similar verse about taking desire as a god, without the mention of knowledge.

hadith.gist: Those who love one another for Allah's sake will be on pulpits of light on the Day of Judgment, admired even by prophets.
The Prophet was always smiling and often joked, yet never took serious matters lightly.

maxims: These recommendations are not bulletproof, but you must do them
Respond does not mean flawless; it means your best
Love is not just an emotion; it needs proof
Who you spend your time with is life's most important decision
Even if you are losing the fight, put it up

stories.who: Hud's people and the jinn who listened
stories.point: Effort does not determine response; those you never addressed may believe.
He did everything right and still did not get the response he wanted.
Materialist logic judges by power and fluency, and mocking what someone cannot control is low.

contemporary: Running masjids and community work like businesses
Blind optimism in the community that ignores visible deficits
The political tactic of digging up an opponent's past instead of answering the argument
takeaways: Follow the recommendations of dawah and avoid its pitfalls, then leave the results to Allah
Respond to Allah's commands now, as fully as you can, while repentance is still open
Choose and keep friends who help you get closer to Allah, and prove that love through action
Never mock traits people cannot control, and argue with ideas, not persons
Check whether your desires have become what you obey, especially as your knowledge grows

35:41.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمۡسِكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَن تَزُولَاۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَهُمَا مِنۡ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
35:41.en: Lo! Allah graspeth the heavens and the earth that they deviate not, and if they were to deviate there is not one that could grasp them after Him. Lo! He is ever Clement, Forgiving

36:38.ar: وَٱلشَّمۡسُ تَجۡرِي لِمُسۡتَقَرࣲّ لَّهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
36:38.en: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

48:7.ar: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
48:7.en: Allah's are the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

8:11.ar: إِذۡ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِۦ وَيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمۡ رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيَرۡبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلۡأَقۡدَامَ
8:11.en: When He made the slumber fall upon you as a reassurance from him and sent down water from the sky upon you, that thereby He might purify you, and remove from you the fear of Satan, and make strong your hearts and firm (your) feet thereby

8:43.ar: إِذۡ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡ أَرَىٰكَهُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّفَشِلۡتُمۡ وَلَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَلَّمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
8:43.en: When Allah showed them unto thee (O Muhammad) in thy dream as few in number, and if He had shown them to thee as many, ye (Muslims) would have faltered and would have quarrelled over the affair. But Allah saved (you). Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

8:44.ar: وَإِذۡ يُرِيكُمُوهُمۡ إِذِ ٱلۡتَقَيۡتُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِكُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ لِيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ اۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
8:44.en: And when He made you (Muslims), when ye met (them), see them with your eyes as few, and lessened you in their eyes, (it was) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done. Unto Allah all things are brought back

8:10.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ بِهِۦ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
8:10.en: Allah appointed it only as good tidings, and that your hearts thereby might be at rest. Victory cometh only by the help of Allah. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise

33:25.ar: وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيۡظِهِمۡ لَمۡ يَنَالُواْ خَيۡرࣰ اۚ وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزࣰ ا
33:25.en: And Allah repulsed the disbelievers in their wrath; they gained no good. Allah averted their attack from the believers. Allah is ever Strong, Mighty

30:5.ar: بِنَصۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
30:5.en: In Allah's help to victory. He helpeth to victory whom He will. He is the Mighty, the Merciful

27:9.ar: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
27:9.en: O Moses! Lo! it is I, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

4:158.ar: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡهِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:158.en: But Allah took him up unto Himself. Allah was ever Mighty, Wise

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

5:117.ar: مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِي بِهِۦٓ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمۡۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
5:117.en: I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them. Thou art Witness over all things

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

4:139.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۚ أَيَبۡتَغُونَ عِندَهُمُ ٱلۡعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ ٱلۡعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا
4:139.en: Those who chose disbelievers for their friends instead of believers! Do they look for power at their hands? Lo! all power appertaineth to Allah

79:24.en: And proclaimed: "I (Pharaoh) am your Lord the Highest

43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers flowing under me? Can ye not then discern

10:92.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنۡ خَلۡفَكَ ءَايَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ
10:92.en: But this day We save thee in thy body that thou mayst be a portent for those after thee. Lo! most of mankind are heedless of Our portents

PLqHfgmsBUw.speaker: adnan
PLqHfgmsBUw.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice; refers to his twelve categories of names
PLqHfgmsBUw.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Aziz (The Unfathomable)
PLqHfgmsBUw.one_line: Al-'Aziz as the unreachable, undefeatable Almighty, and how His servant carries dignity, humility before Allah, and protects others' dignity.
PLqHfgmsBUw.summary: Opening the category of Allah's highness, he renders Al-'Aziz as the Unfathomable: the One with no real opponent, never defeated, who grants dignity, and who cannot be grasped by the mind. He notes how the Quran pairs it with the Wise, the Merciful, the Strong and the Knowing so that absolute power never suggests recklessness, cruelty or oppression. A God you could fully break down would not be God, he argues. He then shows the name closing passages about things we cannot explain: the soldiers of Allah at Badr and the Trench, His speaking to Musa, Isa's ascension, the pursuers standing at the cave without seeing the Prophet, and Isa's plea on Judgment Day that the Prophet repeated all night. Being a servant of Al-'Aziz means walking with self-respect, as Sumayyah, Ammar and Bilal did under torture. He gives three applications: seek dignity only from Allah and never sell yourself through alliances with oppressors or chasing money, expecting to be tested before it pays off; come to Allah in humble submission and accept that much of Him is beyond reach; and protect other people's dignity, even those who once wronged you, because whoever strips another of dignity will have his own taken by Allah.

outline.heading: Meanings of Al-'Aziz
outline.gist: A name of hope and strength with several definitions: without real opponent, never beaten, granter of dignity, and the One who cannot be comprehended.

outline.heading: A name of highness and its frequency
outline.gist: Contemplating names in groups helps; Al-'Aziz appears about 95 times, most often paired with Al-Hakim.

outline.heading: Why it is paired with Wise, Merciful, Strong and Knowing
outline.gist: Each pairing reassures: unquestionable power does not mean recklessness, cruelty, borrowed strength or ignorant oppression.

outline.heading: He holds the heavens and earth from ceasing
outline.gist: If they ceased, no one but Him could bring them back.

outline.heading: The sun's appointed course
outline.gist: Its precise path is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the four birds
outline.gist: Ibrahim asked to see how the dead are revived; the lesson ends with Al-'Aziz because we will never understand how it works and that is fine.

outline.heading: Anything you can fully understand is not God
outline.gist: An umbrella name: belief in a Creator requires that He is beyond full comprehension.

outline.heading: His soldiers at Badr: rain, sleep, dreams and perception
outline.gist: Victory came through rain, drowsiness, a dream, and controlling how each army perceived the other's numbers.

outline.heading: The Trench: a drop in temperature and some wind
outline.gist: Ten thousand who marched to destroy Madinah left because of cold and wind.

outline.heading: Every great victory ends with this name
outline.gist: Angels were only for morale; victory comes from Allah the Almighty, who sent the confederates back empty-handed and spared the believers fighting.

outline.heading: Allah speaking to Musa
outline.gist: No one can explain how that speech worked, so it is introduced with 'I am Allah, the Almighty, the Wise'.

outline.heading: Isa raised up and the pursuers at the cave
outline.gist: Isa's ascension and the Quraysh reaching the very cave yet not looking in are events beyond explanation.

outline.heading: Isa's plea on Judgment Day and the Prophet's night of one verse
outline.gist: Isa says if You forgive them You are the Almighty, the Wise; the Prophet repeated this verse all night, a source of hope since no one questions Allah's forgiveness.

outline.heading: The servant of Al-'Aziz carries dignity
outline.gist: Ask with integrity and walk the earth with self-respect that refuses self-humiliation.

outline.heading: Sumayyah and Ammar under torture
outline.gist: Sumayyah never broke and became Islam's first martyr; Ammar said words under coercion and the Prophet reassured him his heart full of faith was what mattered.

outline.heading: Bilal: 'One, One' under the boulder
outline.gist: His refusal to be broken became the slogan Muslims chose at Badr.

outline.heading: Living the name 1: all dignity belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Those who ally with oppressors seeking strength only gain humiliation; those who refuse, even when they bleed, have more dignity.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's borrowed glory
outline.gist: He claimed to be the highest lord and owner of Egypt's rivers, then the sea closed over him and his body was left as a sign.

outline.heading: Do not sell yourself for money or position
outline.gist: The slave of money lives in humiliation; seeking dignity through Allah is confidence, not arrogance, and expect repeated rejection as a test of commitment.

outline.heading: Living the name 2: enter the empty door of humility
outline.gist: Every door to Allah is crowded except humbling yourself before Him; accept that the divine is beyond your reach and that this is how you know He is Allah.

outline.heading: Living the name 3: protect others' dignity
outline.gist: Whoever takes another's dignity has it taken by Allah; Ibn Mas'ud said Muslims were dignified from the day Umar embraced Islam.

outline.heading: When you hold power over someone who wronged you
outline.gist: Even out of vengeance, do not strip their dignity; walk with confidence, come to Allah humbly and protect others.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-'Aziz as unreachable, undefeated, granter of dignity, and its Quranic pairings.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: A God you could fully comprehend would not be God.

themes.label: Dignity and self-respect ('izzah)
themes.note: The servant of Al-'Aziz seeks dignity only from Allah and refuses to humiliate himself before people or money.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Sumayyah, Ammar and Bilal as models of unbroken dignity under persecution.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Badr, the Trench and the cave as victories through Allah's unseen soldiers.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Isa's plea gives hope that Allah can forgive even grave sins since no one questions Him.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Approach Allah with humble submission and accept the limits of human comprehension.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: The slave of money gives up dignity and lives miserably.

quran.point: Allah holds the heavens and earth lest they cease
The sun's course is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing
Ibrahim and the birds, ending 'know that Allah is Almighty, Wise'
To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and earth
Rain and drowsiness sent before Badr
The dream and each army seeing the other as few
Angels were glad tidings; victory is only from Allah the Almighty, Wise
The confederates sent back in rage and the believers spared fighting
He grants victory to whom He wills; He is the Almighty
'O Musa, I am Allah, the Almighty, the Wise'
Allah raised Isa to Himself; Allah is Almighty, Wise
The two in the cave; the verse ends with Allah Almighty, Wise
Isa questioned about his worship: 'if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise'
Those who take enemies as allies seeking dignity: all dignity belongs to Allah
Pharaoh's claim to be the highest lord
Pharaoh boasting of Egypt and its rivers
His body preserved as a sign after drowning

hadith.gist: The Prophet spent a whole night reciting one verse over and over: 'If You punish them, they are Your servants; if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise'
Ammar said what the torturers demanded and the Prophet asked how he found his heart; when he said it was full of faith, the Prophet told him to do the same if they returned
Wretched is the slave of the dinar and dirham
A dua asking Allah by His might and the servant's lowliness
Ibn Mas'ud: we have been dignified since the day Umar accepted Islam

maxims: Anything you can understand fully is not God
All dignity belongs to Allah
Every grand victory in the Quran ends with this name
Take someone's dignity and Allah will take yours

stories.point: We need not understand how Allah revives the dead to be certain He does.
Victory came through Allah's unseen soldiers: rain, sleep, dreams and perception.
Cold and wind defeated an army of ten thousand.

stories.who: The Prophet and Abu Bakr in the cave
stories.point: The pursuers came close enough to end the story yet did not look.
Refused to break under torture though permitted to, and became the first martyr.
His cry of 'One, One' under a boulder became the believers' slogan at Badr.
Worldly glory without Allah ends in eternal humiliation.

stories.who: Umar's conversion as told by Ibn Mas'ud
stories.point: Granting others dignity is a lasting gift remembered for a lifetime.

takeaways: Seek dignity only through Allah and never humiliate yourself for a job, position or money
Expect to be tested by rejection when you hold to dignity, and stay committed
Come to Allah in humility, especially in Ramadan, accepting what is beyond your understanding
Protect other people's dignity, even those who once wronged you

2:117.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَإِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
2:117.en: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is

6:101.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ صَٰحِبَةࣱۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
6:101.en: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! How can He have a child, when there is for Him no consort, when He created all things and is Aware of all things

13:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّكُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ
13:2.en: Allah it is Who raised up the heavens without visible supports, then mounted the Throne, and compelled the sun and the moon to be of service, each runneth unto an appointed term; He ordereth the course; He detaileth the revelations, that haply ye may be certain of the meeting with your Lord

13:3.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣰ اۖ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
13:3.en: And He it is Who spread out the earth and placed therein firm hills and flowing streams, and of all fruits He placed therein two spouses (male and female). He covereth the night with the day. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought

13:4.ar: وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قِطَعࣱ مُّتَجَٰوِرَٰتࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣱ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَزَرۡعࣱ وَنَخِيلࣱ صِنۡوَانࣱ وَغَيۡرُ صِنۡوَانࣲ يُسۡقَىٰ بِمَآءࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعۡضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فِي ٱلۡأُكُلِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
13:4.en: And in the Earth are neighbouring tracts, vineyards and ploughed lands, and date-palms, like and unlike, which are watered with one water. And we have made some of them to excel others in fruit. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who have sense

25:45.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنࣰ ا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلࣰ ا
25:45.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread the shade - And if He willed He could have made it still - then We have made the sun its pilot

25:46.ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡنَا قَبۡضࣰ ا يَسِيرࣰ ا
25:46.en: Then We withdraw it unto Us, a gradual withdrawal

25:47.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ لِبَاسࣰ ا وَٱلنَّوۡمَ سُبَاتࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورࣰ ا
25:47.en: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection

25:48.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشۡرَۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ طَهُورࣰ ا
25:48.en: And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy, and We send down purifying water from the sky

25:49.ar: لِّنُحۡـِۧيَ بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ ا وَنُسۡقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقۡنَآ أَنۡعَٰمࣰ ا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:49.en: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof

16:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:3.en: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. High be He Exalted above all that they associate (with Him)

16:4.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
16:4.en: He hath created man from a drop of fluid, yet behold! he is an open opponent

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And wherein is beauty for you, when ye bring them home, and when ye take them out to pasture

16:7.ar: وَتَحۡمِلُ أَثۡقَالَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلۡأَنفُسِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:7.en: And they bear your loads for you unto a land ye could not reach save with great trouble to yourselves. Lo! your Lord is Full of Pity, Merciful

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:8.en: And horses and mules and asses (hath He created) that ye may ride them, and for ornament. And He createth that which ye know not

16:9.ar: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرࣱۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
16:9.en: And Allah's is the direction of the way, and some (roads) go not straight. And had He willed He would have led you all aright

16:10.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰۖ لَّكُم مِّنۡهُ شَرَابࣱ وَمِنۡهُ شَجَرࣱ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
16:10.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, whence ye have drink, and whence are trees on which ye send your beasts to pasture

16:11.ar: يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرۡعَ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:11.en: Therewith He causeth crops to grow for you, and the olive and the date-palm and grapes and all kinds of fruit. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for people who reflect

16:12.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ وَٱلنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَٰتُۢ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
16:12.en: And He hath constrained the night and the day and the sun and the moon to be of service unto you, and the stars are made subservient by His command. Lo! herein indeed are portents for people who have sense

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants

50:6.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَيۡفَ بَنَيۡنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجࣲ‏
50:6.en: Have they not then observed the sky above them, how We have constructed it and beautified it, and how there are no rifts therein

50:7.ar: وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجِۭ بَهِيجࣲ‏
50:7.en: And the earth have We spread out, and have flung firm hills therein, and have caused of every lovely kind to grow thereon

50:8.en: A vision and a reminder for every penitent slave

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, and therewith We bring forth buds of every kind; We bring forth the green blade from which We bring forth the thick-clustered grain; and from the date-palm, from the pollen thereof, spring pendant bunches; and (We bring forth) gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, alike and unlike. Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who believe

12:18.ar: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمࣲ كَذِبࣲۚ قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلࣱۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُسۡتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
12:18.en: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience. And Allah it is Whose help is to be sought in that (predicament) which ye describe

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

15:85.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَأٓتِيَةࣱۖ فَٱصۡفَحِ ٱلصَّفۡحَ ٱلۡجَمِيلَ
15:85.en: We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them save with truth, and lo! the Hour is surely coming. So forgive, (O Muhammad), with a gracious forgiveness

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame

35:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُوْلِيٓ أَجۡنِحَةࣲ مَّثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۚ يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
35:1.en: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four. He multiplieth in creation what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen, and the good things of His providing? Say: Such, on the Day of Resurrection, will be only for those who believed during the life of the world. Thus do we detail Our revelations for people who have knowledge

w-nyJFcGYlw.speaker: adnan
w-nyJFcGYlw.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice; personal anecdote about a residency interview in Halifax
w-nyJFcGYlw.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Badi' (The Innovator)
w-nyJFcGYlw.one_line: Al-Badi', the One who originated all creation without precedent, and how it calls us to notice beauty and act beautifully.
w-nyJFcGYlw.summary: Continuing the names of creation, he presents Al-Badi' as the One who invented everything with no previous example. Human creativity, however brilliant, always copies or recombines patterns Allah already made, and our first attempts are rarely good, while Allah needed no model or practice. Most of the talk walks through Quranic passages that list the beauty of creation: the raised heavens, the earth's gardens irrigated by one water yet differing in taste, the moving shade, livestock and horses, the sea and stars. He argues that witnessing this beauty is one of the great gifts of being alive, available every sunrise and the reason people love to travel, and that even the smallest creatures the Quraysh mocked reveal astonishing detail. From the hadith that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, he extends beauty from appearance to conduct: beautiful patience, a beautiful divorce, forgiving without a last humiliating word, and parting ways with partners or friends gracefully. He ends with two ways to live the name: channel creativity into serving people rather than inventing new rituals or forbidding what Allah allowed, and pause to appreciate the colours and sounds of the world as the Prophet did, staying connected to the creation around us.

outline.heading: Al-Badi' within the names of creation
outline.gist: He places the name within his twelve categories of Allah's names and describes it as a name about beauty.

outline.heading: Meaning: inventing with no previous example
outline.gist: Al-Badi' appears twice in the Quran, as Originator of the heavens and earth who only says 'be'; it means creating creatively without any precedent.

outline.heading: All human invention is imitation
outline.gist: Planes, helicopters and submarines copy designs Allah made; the most creative people recombine His patterns, which should deepen appreciation of His magnificence.

outline.heading: No first drafts for Allah
outline.gist: Human first attempts are usually poor and need practice, but Allah innovated everything without coaching or repeated attempts.

outline.heading: Surat al-Ra'd: heavens without pillars, gardens of one water
outline.gist: Raised skies, subjected sun and moon, mountains and rivers, and neighbouring plots watered alike yet differing in taste, as signs for those who think.

outline.heading: Surat al-Furqan: shade, night, rest and rain
outline.gist: The shade moved by the sun, night for rest, day for living, and winds and rain that revive dead land.

outline.heading: Surat an-Nahl: livestock, horses, water, the sea and stars
outline.gist: A long passage on blessings that carry warmth, food, beauty and transport, ending with the sea, mountains, paths and stars made to serve people.

outline.heading: His innovation is endless
outline.gist: If you counted Allah's blessings you could never finish; the more we look and search, the more of His invention we find.

outline.heading: Witnessing beauty is a gift of being alive
outline.gist: Step outside and look at the colours of the dawn horizon; His creation is always at your fingertips and never grows boring.

outline.heading: Travel and the first sight of the ocean
outline.gist: People love travel because they see new parts of creation; he recalls being stunned by the Atlantic in Halifax and saying subhanallah beside his aunt.

outline.heading: The parable of the mosquito and the insect surahs
outline.gist: The Quraysh mocked a Lord who speaks of ants, spiders and bees; today the systems inside tiny creatures should increase our awe of His invention.

outline.heading: Look at the sky, the earth and the ripening fruit
outline.gist: Verses on a flawless adorned sky and gardens as insight for every returning heart, and the command to watch fruit as it forms and ripens.

outline.heading: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
outline.gist: The context of trailing garments as a show of status and arrogance, and the companions' question about fine clothes and shoes; Allah loves to see His blessing on His servant.

outline.heading: Al-Badi' as the producer of beauty: behave beautifully
outline.gist: Beautiful is a description rather than a name, but part of this name; Allah asks for beautiful appearance and beautiful conduct.

outline.heading: Beautiful patience
outline.gist: Ya'qub's patience shows one can persevere while staying optimistic and working toward a goal instead of being grumpy and broken.

outline.heading: Even divorce must be beautiful
outline.gist: The Quran asks for a beautiful release in separation, not only in marriage.

outline.heading: Forgive beautifully
outline.gist: Do not deliver one last piece of your mind before forgiving; forgive without humiliating the other person.

outline.heading: Parting ways beautifully
outline.gist: When friends or partners cannot work together, part on that matter without ending the friendship.

outline.heading: Surat al-Mulk: look again for a flaw
outline.gist: The seven heavens show no defect however many times you look; the sky is adorned with lamps.

outline.heading: Surat Fatir: angels with wings
outline.gist: The Originator released creation and made angels messengers with wings, adding to creation as He wills because there is beauty in it.

outline.heading: The Prophet sees Jibril in his true form
outline.gist: Jibril filling the horizon with hundreds of wings, and at the Ascension appearing like a worn cloth out of reverence for Allah.

outline.heading: Living the name: innovate in service, not in religion
outline.gist: Be creative in making people's lives easier, but do not invent rituals, self-harm as worship, or forbid the adornments Allah permitted.

outline.heading: Living the name: appreciate the beauty around you
outline.gist: Children hearing for the first time, birdsong, and the Muslim's rituals tied to sun, moon, rain and thunder; the Prophet was deeply connected to the world around him.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Badi' as originating creation without precedent and as the producer of beauty.

themes.label: Beauty: noticing it and producing it
themes.note: The Quran repeatedly tells people to look at the beauty of creation; seeing it is one of the great gifts of life.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Beauty in conduct: patience, divorce, forgiveness and parting ways all done gracefully.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: The blessings of an-Nahl cannot be counted and are listed so people will be grateful.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgive without a final humiliating word.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Creativity must not invent new rituals, self-harm or bans on what Allah made lawful.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His strong connection to and appreciation of the world around him.

quran.point: Originator of the heavens and earth who only says 'be' and it is
The Originator has no son and no spouse and created everything
Heavens raised without pillars and gardens watered alike yet differing in taste
The moving shade, night for rest, winds and rain as signs of His design
Livestock, horses, water, sea, mountains and stars, and blessings too many to count
Allah is not shy to give the parable of a mosquito or what is beyond it
The flawless sky and the beautiful plants as insight for every returning servant
Olives and pomegranates alike and unlike: look at the fruit as it ripens
Beautiful patience
A beautiful release when separating
Pardon with a beautiful pardon
Look again and you will find no flaw in the heavens, adorned with lamps
Angels as messengers with wings; He adds to creation as He wills
Who dares forbid the adornments Allah brought forth for His servants

hadith.gist: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, said when companions asked whether liking fine clothes and shoes was arrogance
The warning against garments that trail behind out of arrogance
The Prophet saw Jibril twice in his true form, with hundreds of wings filling the horizon
On the night of the Ascension Jibril looked like a worn-out cloth out of reverence for Allah

maxims: Everything we make is some degree of repetition
Your search for a deficit will come back empty
Be innovative in service, not in religion

stories.who: His first sight of the ocean in Halifax
stories.point: Encountering a new part of creation stirs awe that makes the tongue glorify Allah spontaneously.

stories.who: The Quraysh mocking surahs named after insects
stories.point: What they found trivial reveals intricate design that should increase our appreciation of Allah.
Patience can be beautiful: steady and hopeful rather than bitter.
Angels' wings reflect beauty in creation, and Jibril's humbled appearance shows reverence for Allah.

contemporary: Videos of children hearing for the first time with hearing aids
takeaways: Take a few moments each day, such as at sunrise, to notice the beauty of Allah's creation
Look good and take care of yourself as a sign of Allah's blessing, without arrogance
Make your patience, forgiveness and partings beautiful
Use creativity to serve people and make their lives easier, never to add to the religion
Reconnect with the natural world as the Prophet did

5:109.ar: ۞يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَآ أُجِبۡتُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:109.en: In the day when Allah gathereth together the messengers, and saith: What was your response (from mankind)? they say: We have no knowledge. Lo! Thou, only Thou art the Knower of Things Hidden

5:110.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱذۡكُرۡ نِعۡمَتِي عَلَيۡكَ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَتِكَ إِذۡ أَيَّدتُّكَ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِي ٱلۡمَهۡدِ وَكَهۡلࣰ اۖ وَإِذۡ عَلَّمۡتُكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَۖ وَإِذۡ تَخۡلُقُ مِنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيۡـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيۡرِ بِإِذۡنِي فَتَنفُخُ فِيهَا فَتَكُونُ طَيۡرَۢا بِإِذۡنِيۖ وَتُبۡرِئُ ٱلۡأَكۡمَهَ وَٱلۡأَبۡرَصَ بِإِذۡنِيۖ وَإِذۡ تُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ بِإِذۡنِيۖ وَإِذۡ كَفَفۡتُ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَنكَ إِذۡ جِئۡتَهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
5:110.en: When Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Remember My favour unto thee and unto thy mother; how I strengthened thee with the holy Spirit, so that thou spakest unto mankind in the cradle as in maturity; and how I taught thee the Scripture and Wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and how thou didst shape of clay as it were the likeness of a bird by My permission, and didst blow upon it and it was a bird by My permission, and thou didst heal him who was born blind and the leper by My permission; and how thou didst raise the dead by My permission; and how I restrained the Children of Israel from (harming) thee when thou camest unto them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved exclaimed: This is naught else than mere magic

5:111.ar: وَإِذۡ أَوۡحَيۡتُ إِلَى ٱلۡحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ أَنۡ ءَامِنُواْ بِي وَبِرَسُولِي قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَٱشۡهَدۡ بِأَنَّنَا مُسۡلِمُونَ
5:111.en: And when I inspired the disciples, (saying): Believe in Me and in My messenger, they said: We believe. Bear witness that we have surrendered (unto Thee) "we are muslims

5:112.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ ٱلۡحَوَارِيُّونَ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ هَلۡ يَسۡتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا مَآئِدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ قَالَ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:112.en: When the disciples said: O Jesus, son of Mary! Is thy Lord able to send down for us a table spread with food from heaven? He said: Observe your duty to Allah, if ye are true believers

5:113.ar: قَالُواْ نُرِيدُ أَن نَّأۡكُلَ مِنۡهَا وَتَطۡمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا وَنَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ صَدَقۡتَنَا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيۡهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
5:113.en: (They said:) We wish to eat thereof, that we may satisfy our hearts and know that thou hast spoken truth to us, and that thereof we may be witnesses

5:114.ar: قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ ٱللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَآ أَنزِلۡ عَلَيۡنَا مَآئِدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدࣰ ا لِّأَوَّلِنَا وَءَاخِرِنَا وَءَايَةࣰ مِّنكَۖ وَٱرۡزُقۡنَا وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
5:114.en: Jesus, son of Mary, said: O Allah, Lord of us! Send down for us a table spread with food from heaven, that it may be a feast for us, for the first of us and for the last of us, and a sign from Thee. Give us sustenance, for Thou art the Best of Sustainers

5:115.ar: قَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بَعۡدُ مِنكُمۡ فَإِنِّيٓ أُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابࣰ ا لَّآ أُعَذِّبُهُۥٓ أَحَدࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
5:115.en: Allah said: Lo! I send it down for you. And whoso disbelieveth of you afterward, him surely will I punish with a punishment wherewith I have not punished any of (My) creatures

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

5:117.ar: مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِي بِهِۦٓ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمۡۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
5:117.en: I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them. Thou art Witness over all things

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

5:119.ar: قَالَ ٱللَّهُ هَٰذَا يَوۡمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ صِدۡقُهُمۡۚ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣱ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۖ رَّضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
5:119.en: Allah saith: This is a day in which their truthfulness profiteth the truthful, for theirs are Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they are secure for ever, Allah taking pleasure in them and they in Him. That is the great triumph

5:120.ar: لِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا فِيهِنَّۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرُۢ
5:120.en: Unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is therein, and He is Able to do all things

6:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ وَٱلنُّورَۖ ثُمَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ يَعۡدِلُونَ
6:1.en: Praise be to Allah, Who hath created the heavens and the earth, and hath appointed darkness and light. Yet those who disbelieve ascribe rivals unto their Lord

6:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن طِينࣲ ثُمَّ قَضَىٰٓ أَجَلࣰ اۖ وَأَجَلࣱ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُۥۖ ثُمَّ أَنتُمۡ تَمۡتَرُونَ
6:2.en: He it is Who hath created you from clay, and hath decreed a term for you. A term is fixed with Him. Yet still ye doubt

6:3.ar: وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَعۡلَمُ سِرَّكُمۡ وَجَهۡرَكُمۡ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَكۡسِبُونَ
6:3.en: He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth. He knoweth both your secret and your utterance, and He knoweth what ye earn

6:4.ar: وَمَا تَأۡتِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةࣲ مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ إِلَّا كَانُواْ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضِينَ
6:4.en: Never came there unto them a revelation of the revelations of Allah but they did turn away from it

6:5.ar: فَقَدۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِيهِمۡ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُاْ مَا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
6:5.en: And they denied the truth when it came unto them. But there will come unto them the tidings of that which they used to deride

6:6.ar: أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن قَرۡنࣲ مَّكَّنَّٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَا لَمۡ نُمَكِّن لَّكُمۡ وَأَرۡسَلۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡهِم مِّدۡرَارࣰ ا وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهِمۡ فَأَهۡلَكۡنَٰهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمۡ وَأَنشَأۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ قَرۡنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
6:6.en: See they not how many a generation We destroyed before them, whom We had established in the earth more firmly than We have established you, and We shed on them abundant showers from the sky, and made the rivers flow beneath them. Yet we destroyed them for their sins, and created after them another generation

6:7.ar: وَلَوۡ نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ كِتَٰبࣰ ا فِي قِرۡطَاسࣲ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ لَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
6:7.en: Had we sent down unto thee (Muhammad) (actual) writing upon parchment, so that they could feel it with their hands, those who disbelieve would have said: This is naught else than mere magic

6:8.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَكࣱۖ وَلَوۡ أَنزَلۡنَا مَلَكࣰ ا لَّقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنظَرُونَ
6:8.en: They say: Why hath not an angel been sent down unto him? If We sent down an angel, then the matter would be judged; no further time would be allowed them (for reflection)

6:9.ar: وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ مَلَكࣰ ا لَّجَعَلۡنَٰهُ رَجُلࣰ ا وَلَلَبَسۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم مَّا يَلۡبِسُونَ
6:9.en: Had we appointed him (Our messenger) an angel, We assuredly had made him (as) a man (that he might speak to men); and (thus) obscured for them (the truth) they (now) obscure

6:10.ar: وَلَقَدِ ٱسۡتُهۡزِئَ بِرُسُلࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
6:10.en: Messengers (of Allah) have been derided before thee, but that whereat they scoffed surrounded such of them as did deride

6:11.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ
6:11.en: Say (unto the disbelievers): Travel in the land, and see the nature of the consequence for the rejecters

6:12.ar: قُل لِّمَن مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُل لِّلَّهِۚ كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَۚ لَيَجۡمَعَنَّكُمۡ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:12.en: Say: Unto whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: Unto Allah. He hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that He may bring you all together to the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. Those who ruin their souls will not believe

6:13.ar: ۞وَلَهُۥ مَا سَكَنَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
6:13.en: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever resteth in the night and the day. He is the Hearer, the Knower

6:14.ar: قُلۡ أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيࣰّ ا فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَهُوَ يُطۡعِمُ وَلَا يُطۡعَمُۗ قُلۡ إِنِّيٓ أُمِرۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنۡ أَسۡلَمَۖ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
6:14.en: Say: Shall I choose for a protecting friend other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who feedeth and is never fed? Say: I am ordered to be the first to surrender (unto Him). And be not thou (O Muhammad) of the idolaters

6:15.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ إِنۡ عَصَيۡتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
6:15.en: Say: I fear, if I rebel against my Lord, the retribution of an Awful Day

6:16.ar: مَّن يُصۡرَفۡ عَنۡهُ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ فَقَدۡ رَحِمَهُۥۚ وَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
6:16.en: He from whom (such retribution) is averted on that day, (Allah) hath in truth had mercy on him. That will be the signal triumph

6:17.ar: وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرࣲّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُۥٓ إِلَّا هُوَۖ وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ بِخَيۡرࣲ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
6:17.en: If Allah touch thee with affliction, there is none that can relieve therefrom save Him, and if He touch thee with good fortune (there is none that can impair it); for He is Able to do all things

6:18.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:18.en: He is the Omnipotent over His slaves, and He is the Wise, the Knower

14:19.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِن يَشَأۡ يُذۡهِبۡكُمۡ وَيَأۡتِ بِخَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدࣲ‏
14:19.en: Hast thou not seen that Allah hath created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He will, He can remove you and bring (in) some new creation

14:20.en: And that is no great matter for Allah

14:21.ar: وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَقَالَ ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُاْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمۡ تَبَعࣰ ا فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّغۡنُونَ عَنَّا مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ قَالُواْ لَوۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَيۡنَٰكُمۡۖ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡنَآ أَجَزِعۡنَآ أَمۡ صَبَرۡنَا مَا لَنَا مِن مَّحِيصࣲ‏
14:21.en: They all come forth unto their Lord. Then those who were despised say unto those who were scornful: We were unto you a following, can ye then avert from us aught of Allah's doom? They say: Had Allah guided us, we should have guided you. Whether we rage or patiently endure is (now) all one for us; we have no place of refuge

14:22.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوۡتُكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِيۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۖ مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصۡرِخِكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصۡرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرۡتُ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكۡتُمُونِ مِن قَبۡلُۗ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
14:22.en: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

14:23.ar: وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهِمۡۖ تَحِيَّتُهُمۡ فِيهَا سَلَٰمٌ
14:23.en: And those who believed and did good works are made to enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow, therein abiding by permission of their Lord, their greeting therein: Peace

14:24.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلࣰ ا كَلِمَةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰ كَشَجَرَةࣲ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصۡلُهَا ثَابِتࣱ وَفَرۡعُهَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
14:24.en: Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven

14:25.ar: تُؤۡتِيٓ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينِۭ بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهَاۗ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
14:25.en: Giving its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord? Allah coineth the similitudes for mankind in order that they may reflect

14:26.ar: وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةࣲ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ٱجۡتُثَّتۡ مِن فَوۡقِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارࣲ‏
14:26.en: And the similitude of a bad saying is as a bad tree, uprooted from upon the earth, possessing no stability

14:27.ar: يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَۚ وَيَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ
14:27.en: Allah confirmeth those who believe by a firm saying in the life of the world and in the Hereafter, and Allah sendeth wrong-doers astray. And Allah doeth what He will

14:28.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ بَدَّلُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ كُفۡرࣰ ا وَأَحَلُّواْ قَوۡمَهُمۡ دَارَ ٱلۡبَوَارِ
14:28.en: Hast thou not seen those who gave the grace of Allah in exchange for thanklessness and led their people down to the Abode of Loss

14:29.en: (Even to) hell? They are exposed thereto. A hapless end

14:30.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا لِّيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۗ قُلۡ تَمَتَّعُواْ فَإِنَّ مَصِيرَكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ
14:30.en: And they set up rivals to Allah that they may mislead (men) from His way. Say: Enjoy life (while ye may) for lo! your journey's end will be the Fire

14:31.ar: قُل لِّعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ سِرࣰّ ا وَعَلَانِيَةࣰ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا بَيۡعࣱ فِيهِ وَلَا خِلَٰلٌ
14:31.en: Tell My bondmen who believe to establish worship and spend of that which We have given them, secretly and publicly, before a day cometh wherein there will be neither traffick nor befriending

14:32.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ لِتَجۡرِيَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ
14:32.en: Allah is He Who created the heavens and the earth, and causeth water to descend from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you, and maketh the ships to be of service unto you, that they may run upon the sea at His command, and hath made of service unto you the rivers

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ
14:33.en: And maketh the sun and the moon, constant in their courses, to be of service unto you, and hath made of service unto you the night and the day

14:34.ar: وَءَاتَىٰكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُۚ وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَظَلُومࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
14:34.en: And He giveth you of all ye ask of Him, and if ye would count the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! man is verily a wrong-doer, an ingrate

16:65.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَسۡمَعُونَ
16:65.en: Allah sendeth down water from the sky and therewith reviveth the earth after her death. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for a folk who hear

16:66.ar: وَإِنَّ لَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ لَعِبۡرَةࣰۖ نُّسۡقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِۦ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ فَرۡثࣲ وَدَمࣲ لَّبَنًا خَالِصࣰ ا سَآئِغࣰ ا لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ
16:66.en: And lo! in the cattle there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink of that which is in their bellies, from betwixt the refuse and the blood, pure milk palatable to the drinkers

16:67.ar: وَمِن ثَمَرَٰتِ ٱلنَّخِيلِ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنۡهُ سَكَرࣰ ا وَرِزۡقًا حَسَنًاۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
16:67.en: And of the fruits of the date-palm, and grapes, whence ye derive strong drink and (also) good nourishment. Lo! therein is indeed a portent for people who have sense

16:68.ar: وَأَوۡحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلنَّحۡلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي مِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ بُيُوتࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعۡرِشُونَ
16:68.en: And thy Lord inspired the bee, saying: Choose thou habitations in the hills and in the trees and in that which they thatch

16:69.ar: ثُمَّ كُلِي مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ فَٱسۡلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلࣰ اۚ يَخۡرُجُ مِنۢ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابࣱ مُّخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥ فِيهِ شِفَآءࣱ لِّلنَّاسِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:69.en: Then eat of all fruits, and follow the ways of thy Lord, made smooth (for thee). There cometh forth from their bellies a drink divers of hues, wherein is healing for mankind. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for people who reflect

16:70.ar: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمۡۚ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرۡذَلِ ٱلۡعُمُرِ لِكَيۡ لَا يَعۡلَمَ بَعۡدَ عِلۡمࣲ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمࣱ قَدِيرࣱ‏
16:70.en: And Allah createth you, then causeth you to die, and among you is he who is brought back to the most abject stage of life, so that he knoweth nothing after (having had) knowledge. Lo! Allah is Knower, Powerful

16:71.ar: وَٱللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعۡضَكُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فِي ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُواْ بِرَآدِّي رِزۡقِهِمۡ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌۚ أَفَبِنِعۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِ يَجۡحَدُونَ
16:71.en: And Allah hath favoured some of you above others in provision. Now those who are more favoured will by no means hand over their provision to those (slaves) whom their right hands possess, so that they may be equal with them in respect thereof. Is it then the grace of Allah that they deny

16:72.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُم بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةࣰ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِۚ أَفَبِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ يُؤۡمِنُونَ وَبِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ هُمۡ يَكۡفُرُونَ
16:72.en: And Allah hath given you wives of your own kind, and hath given you, from your wives, sons and grandsons, and hath made provision of good things for you. Is it then in vanity that they believe and in the grace of Allah that they disbelieve

16:73.ar: وَيَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ رِزۡقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
16:73.en: And they worship beside Allah that which owneth no provision whatsoever for them from the heavens or the earth, nor have they (whom they worship) any power

16:74.ar: فَلَا تَضۡرِبُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡثَالَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:74.en: So coin not similitudes for Allah. Lo! Allah knoweth; ye know not

35:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُوْلِيٓ أَجۡنِحَةࣲ مَّثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۚ يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
35:1.en: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four. He multiplieth in creation what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

35:2.ar: مَّا يَفۡتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحۡمَةࣲ فَلَا مُمۡسِكَ لَهَاۖ وَمَا يُمۡسِكۡ فَلَا مُرۡسِلَ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
35:2.en: That which Allah openeth unto mankind of mercy none can withhold it; and that which He withholdeth none can release thereafter. He is the Mighty, the Wise

35:3.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ هَلۡ مِنۡ خَٰلِقٍ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
