35:3.en: O mankind! Remember Allah's grace toward you! Is there any creator other than Allah who provideth for you from the sky and the earth? There is no Allah save Him. Whither then are ye turned

35:4.ar: وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدۡ كُذِّبَتۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
35:4.en: And if they deny thee, (O Muhammad), messengers (of Allah) were denied before thee. Unto Allah all things are brought back

35:5.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
35:5.en: O mankind! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. So let not the life of the world beguile you, and let not the (avowed) beguiler beguile you with regard to Allah

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

35:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرٌ
35:7.en: Those who disbelieve, theirs will be an awful doom; and those who believe and do good works, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

35:8.ar: أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ فَرَءَاهُ حَسَنࣰ اۖ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۖ فَلَا تَذۡهَبۡ نَفۡسُكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
35:8.en: Is he, the evil of whose deeds is made fairseeming unto him so that he deemeth it good, (other than Satan's dupe)? Allah verily sendeth whom He will astray, and guideth whom He will; so let not thy soul expire in sighings for them. Lo! Allah is Aware of what they do

35:9.ar: وَٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابࣰ ا فَسُقۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ مَّيِّتࣲ فَأَحۡيَيۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ
35:9.en: And Allah it is Who sendeth the winds and they raise a cloud; then We lead it unto a dead land and revive therewith the earth after its death. Such is the Resurrection

35:10.ar: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلۡعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًاۚ إِلَيۡهِ يَصۡعَدُ ٱلۡكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلۡعَمَلُ ٱلصَّٰلِحُ يَرۡفَعُهُۥۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡكُرُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱۖ وَمَكۡرُ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ
35:10.en: Whoso desireth power (should know that) all power belongeth to Allah. Unto Him good words ascend, and the pious deed doth He exalt; but those who plot iniquities, theirs will be an awful doom; and the plotting of such (folk) will come to naught

35:11.ar: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ اۚ وَمَا تَحۡمِلُ مِنۡ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلۡمِهِۦۚ وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرࣲ وَلَا يُنقَصُ مِنۡ عُمُرِهِۦٓ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبٍۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣱ‏
35:11.en: Allah created you from dust, then from a little fluid, then He made you pairs (the male and female). No female beareth or bringeth forth save with His knowledge. And no-one groweth old who groweth old, nor is aught lessened of his life, but it is recorded in a Book, Lo! that is easy for Allah

35:12.ar: وَمَا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡبَحۡرَانِ هَٰذَا عَذۡبࣱ فُرَاتࣱ سَآئِغࣱ شَرَابُهُۥ وَهَٰذَا مِلۡحٌ أُجَاجࣱۖ وَمِن كُلࣲّ تَأۡكُلُونَ لَحۡمࣰ ا طَرِيࣰّ ا وَتَسۡتَخۡرِجُونَ حِلۡيَةࣰ تَلۡبَسُونَهَاۖ وَتَرَى ٱلۡفُلۡكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ لِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
35:12.en: And the two seas are not alike: this, fresh, sweet, good to drink, this (other) bitter, salt. And from them both ye eat fresh meat and derive the ornament that ye wear. And thou seest the ship cleaving them with its prow that ye may seek of His bounty, and that haply ye may give thanks

35:13.ar: يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مِن قِطۡمِيرٍ
35:13.en: He maketh the night to pass into the day and He maketh the day to pass into the night. He hath subdued the sun and moon to service. Each runneth unto an appointed term. Such is Allah, your Lord; His is the Sovereignty; and those unto whom ye pray instead of Him own not so much as the white spot on a date-stone

35:14.ar: إِن تَدۡعُوهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُواْ دُعَآءَكُمۡ وَلَوۡ سَمِعُواْ مَا ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لَكُمۡۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِشِرۡكِكُمۡۚ وَلَا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثۡلُ خَبِيرࣲ‏
35:14.en: If ye pray unto them they hear not your prayer, and if they heard they could not grant it you. On the Day of Resurrection they will disown association with you. None can inform you like Him Who is Aware

35:15.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
35:15.en: O mankind! Ye are the poor in your relation to Allah. And Allah! He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise

35:16.ar: إِن يَشَأۡ يُذۡهِبۡكُمۡ وَيَأۡتِ بِخَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدࣲ‏
35:16.en: If He will, He can be rid of you and bring (instead of you) some new creation

35:17.en: That is not a hard thing for Allah

35:18.ar: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۚ وَإِن تَدۡعُ مُثۡقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمۡلِهَا لَا يُحۡمَلۡ مِنۡهُ شَيۡءࣱ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰٓۗ إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
35:18.en: And no burdened soul can bear another's burden, and if one heavy laden crieth for (help with) his load, naught of it will be lifted even though he (unto whom he crieth) be of kin. Thou warnest only those who fear their Lord in secret, and have established worship. He who groweth (in goodness), groweth only for himself, (he cannot by his merit redeem others). Unto Allah is the journeying

35:19.en: The blind man is not equal with the seer

35:21.en: Nor is the shadow equal with the sun's full heat

35:22.ar: وَمَا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَحۡيَآءُ وَلَا ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسۡمِعُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُسۡمِعࣲ مَّن فِي ٱلۡقُبُورِ
35:22.en: Nor are the living equal with the dead. Lo! Allah maketh whom He will to hear. Thou canst not reach those who are in the graves

35:24.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ اۚ وَإِن مِّنۡ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيهَا نَذِيرࣱ‏
35:24.en: Lo! We have sent thee with the Truth, a bearer of glad tidings and a warner; and there is not a nation but a warner hath passed among them

n5V1NmFDKug.speaker: adnan
n5V1NmFDKug.speaker_note: Ramadan night prayer at his centre; he gives the two short reminders between sets of rak'ahs and thanks the next imam, Sheikh Ahmad
n5V1NmFDKug.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 23: Third Night of Tahajjud
n5V1NmFDKug.one_line: A tahajjud prayer with two short reminders on ruku' as exaltation of Allah and the Prophet's long, unhurried night prayer, ending with a long witr dua.
n5V1NmFDKug.summary: This is a full night of tahajjud on the twenty-third night of Ramadan. Six rak'ahs are recited from the end of Al-Ma'idah, the opening of Al-An'am, Ibrahim, An-Nahl and Fatir, with two short reminders between the sets. The first is on ruku': the whole unit of prayer takes its name from it because it is the posture of exaltation, so the Prophet told us to glorify the Lord in it, and his own words in it describe every limb, hearing, sight, mind, bones and sinews, humbled before Allah. The second reminder shows how the Prophet stood at night: Hudhayfah prayed behind him as he recited Al-Baqarah, An-Nisa' and Al 'Imran in one rak'ah, slowly, asking for Paradise at its mention and seeking refuge at the mention of punishment, with bowing and prostration nearly as long as the standing, while Ibn Mas'ud nearly sat down from the length. Such prayer, he says, needs love, joy and serenity so that you do not want it to end, like the companion Abbad ibn Bishr who kept praying while struck by arrows rather than cut off his surah. The night closes with a long witr dua for forgiveness, a good ending, the company of the Prophet, pure hearts and relief for the people of Gaza.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation: Isa questioned before the gathered messengers
outline.gist: The closing passage of Al-Ma'idah: Allah's favours to Isa, the table sent down from heaven, and Isa disowning those who worshipped him and his mother.

outline.heading: Recitation: the opening of Al-An'am
outline.gist: Creation from clay, nations destroyed for their sins, Allah has written mercy upon Himself, and none but He removes harm.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ruku' gives the rak'ah its name
outline.gist: The unit of prayer is named after the bowing because of how meaningful it is; the Prophet said to exalt the Lord in it.

outline.heading: Exalting the Lord in ruku'
outline.gist: Ruku' is for glorification and declaring Allah's holiness, with the Prophet's words: Glory be to my Lord the Magnificent, and Most Glorious, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.

outline.heading: Every limb humbled before Allah
outline.gist: The Prophet's dhikr in ruku' names hearing, sight, mind, bones, sinews and all that the feet carry as humbled to the Lord of the worlds.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation: Shaytan disowns his followers and the parable of the good word
outline.gist: The weak and the arrogant blame each other, Shaytan says he only invited them, the good word is like a firmly rooted tree, and Allah's blessings cannot be counted.

outline.heading: Recitation: signs in rain, milk, fruit and the bee
outline.gist: Rain reviving dead land, pure milk from between waste and blood, the bee inspired to build and produce healing honey, and the folly of setting up equals to Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's longer words of glorification in ruku'
outline.gist: Glory to the Possessor of might, dominion, grandeur and majesty; and O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I believe and to You I submit.

outline.heading: Hudhayfah's night: three long surahs in one rak'ah
outline.gist: Hudhayfah expected the Prophet to bow at a hundred verses, but he went on through Al-Baqarah, then An-Nisa', then Al 'Imran.

outline.heading: Ibn Mas'ud nearly sat down behind him
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud said the Prophet stood so long that he resolved to sit and leave him standing alone.

outline.heading: Reciting slowly and answering each verse
outline.gist: He recited unhurriedly, asked for Paradise when it was mentioned and sought refuge at the mention of punishment; his bowing, rising and prostration were each close to the length of his standing.

outline.heading: Long prayer needs love and serenity
outline.gist: Standing that long requires love, joy and a calm in which you do not want the prayer to end.

outline.heading: Abbad ibn Bishr would not cut his surah
outline.gist: Set to guard the camp, he prayed while arrows struck him and told Ammar ibn Yasir he would rather die than break off the surah he was reciting.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation: the mercy no one can hold back
outline.gist: The opening of Fatir: angels with wings as messengers, mercy Allah opens that none can withhold, do not be deceived by this life, and good words rise to Him.

outline.heading: Recitation: you are the ones in need of Allah
outline.gist: The two seas, night entering day, idols that own not a date-skin, all people are poor before Allah, and no soul bears another's burden.

outline.heading: Witr dua: praise befitting His majesty
outline.gist: Abundant praise that fills the heavens and earth, and blessings on the Prophet.

outline.heading: Dua for forgiveness of the sins that change blessings
outline.gist: Asking forgiveness for sins that bring down affliction, change blessings and hold back dua, and for a spacious grave.

outline.heading: Dua to be gathered with the Prophet
outline.gist: Asking to live on his Sunnah, drink from his basin and be raised in his company, and to be looked upon with mercy and accepted.

outline.heading: Dua for a good ending and acceptance
outline.gist: Asking that the best deeds be the last, to meet Allah while He is pleased, and that our meagre offering be accepted.

outline.heading: Dua for the people of Gaza
outline.gist: Asking Allah to lift the affliction from Gaza, spare their blood, feed the hungry, clothe the bare and reward their patience.

outline.heading: Dua for pure hearts and freedom from the Fire
outline.gist: Asking that hearts be cleansed of arrogance, envy and showing off, filled with love of Allah, and that we and our families be freed from the Fire.

outline.heading: Outro

hadith.gist: As for ruku', exalt the Lord in it.
In ruku' the Prophet said: Most Glorious, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.
In ruku' the Prophet said: my hearing, sight, mind, bones, sinews and all my feet carry are humbled before You, Lord of the worlds.
In ruku' the Prophet said: glory to the Possessor of might, dominion, grandeur and majesty.

Hudhayfah prayed with the Prophet at night; he recited Al-Baqarah, An-Nisa' and Al 'Imran slowly in one rak'ah, asking at verses of Paradise and seeking refuge at verses of punishment, with bowing and prostration close to his standing.
Ibn Mas'ud prayed with the Prophet at night and he stood so long that Ibn Mas'ud resolved to sit and leave him.

stories.point: The Prophet's night prayer was long, slow and responsive to every verse.
Even a great companion found the Prophet's standing almost too long, which shows its length.

stories.who: Abbad ibn Bishr and Ammar ibn Yasir guarding the camp
stories.point: Abbad kept praying while hit by arrows rather than break off his surah: the love and serenity that long prayer needs.

contemporary: Gaza: dua for relief and protection of its people
takeaways: Slow down in ruku' and exalt Allah in it with the Prophet's words.
Let the whole body, not only the tongue, be humbled in prayer.
In night prayer recite slowly, asking for Paradise and seeking refuge from punishment as the verses come.
Seek the love and serenity in prayer that make you not want it to end.
